EKF2_ANGERR_INIT.summary: 1-sigma tilt angle uncertainty after gravity vector alignment

EKF2_ARSP_THR.description: Airspeed data is fused for wind estimation if above this threshold. Set to 0 to disable airspeed fusion. For reliable wind estimation both sideslip (see EKF2_FUSE_BETA) and airspeed fusion should be enabled. Only applies to fixed-wing vehicles (or VTOLs in fixed-wing mode).

EKF2_ASPD_MAX.summary: Maximum airspeed used for baro static pressure compensation

EKF2_ASP_DELAY.summary: Airspeed measurement delay relative to IMU measurements

EKF2_AVEL_DELAY.summary: Auxiliary Velocity Estimate delay relative to IMU measurements

EKF2_BARO_CTRL.description: If this parameter is enabled then the estimator will make use of the barometric height measurements to estimate its height in addition to other height sources (if activated).

EKF2_BARO_DELAY.summary: Barometer measurement delay relative to IMU measurements

EKF2_BARO_GATE.summary: Gate size for barometric and GPS height fusion
EKF2_BARO_GATE.description: Sets the number of standard deviations used by the innovation consistency test.

EKF2_BCOEF_X.summary: X-axis ballistic coefficient used for multi-rotor wind estimation
EKF2_BCOEF_X.description: This parameter controls the prediction of drag produced by bluff body drag along the forward/reverse axis when flying a multi-copter which enables estimation of wind drift when enabled by the EKF2_DRAG_CTRL parameter. The drag produced by this effect scales with speed squared. The predicted drag from the rotors is specified separately by the EKF2_MCOEF parameter. Set this parameter to zero to turn off the bluff body drag model for this axis.

EKF2_BCOEF_Y.summary: Y-axis ballistic coefficient used for multi-rotor wind estimation
EKF2_BCOEF_Y.description: This parameter controls the prediction of drag produced by bluff body drag along the right/left axis when flying a multi-copter, which enables estimation of wind drift when enabled by the EKF2_DRAG_CTRL parameter. The drag produced by this effect scales with speed squared. The predicted drag from the rotors is specified separately by the EKF2_MCOEF parameter. Set this parameter to zero to turn off the bluff body drag model for this axis.

EKF2_BETA_GATE.summary: Gate size for synthetic sideslip fusion
EKF2_BETA_GATE.description: Sets the number of standard deviations used by the innovation consistency test.

EKF2_DECL_TYPE.summary: Integer bitmask controlling handling of magnetic declination
EKF2_DECL_TYPE.description: Set bits in the following positions to enable functions. 0 : Set to true to use the declination from the geo_lookup library when the GPS position becomes available, set to false to always use the EKF2_MAG_DECL value. 1 : Set to true to save the EKF2_MAG_DECL parameter to the value returned by the EKF when the vehicle disarms.
choices: Bitmask: 0: use geo_lookup declination, 1: save EKF2_MAG_DECL on disarm

EKF2_DELAY_MAX.summary: Maximum delay of all the aiding sensors
EKF2_DELAY_MAX.description: Defines the delay between the current time and the delayed-time horizon. This value should be at least as large as the largest EKF2_XXX_DELAY parameter.

EKF2_DRAG_CTRL.description: Activate wind speed estimation using specific-force measurements and a drag model defined by EKF2_BCOEF_[XY] and EKF2_MCOEF. Only use on vehicles that have their thrust aligned with the Z axis and no thrust in the XY plane.

EKF2_DRAG_NOISE.summary: Specific drag force observation noise variance
EKF2_DRAG_NOISE.description: Used by the multi-rotor specific drag force model. Increasing this makes the multi-rotor wind estimates adjust more slowly.

EKF2_ENGINE_WRM.summary: Enable constant position fusion during engine warmup
EKF2_ENGINE_WRM.description: When enabled, constant position fusion is enabled when the vehicle is landed and armed. This is intended for IC engine warmup (e.g., fuel engines on catapult) to allow mode transitions to auto/takeoff despite vibrations from running engines.

EKF2_EVA_NOISE.summary: Measurement noise for vision angle measurements
EKF2_EVA_NOISE.description: Used to lower bound or replace the uncertainty included in the message

EKF2_EVP_GATE.summary: Gate size for vision position fusion
EKF2_EVP_GATE.description: Sets the number of standard deviations used by the innovation consistency test.

EKF2_EVP_NOISE.summary: Measurement noise for vision position measurements
EKF2_EVP_NOISE.description: Used to lower bound or replace the uncertainty included in the message

EKF2_EVV_GATE.summary: Gate size for vision velocity estimate fusion
EKF2_EVV_GATE.description: Sets the number of standard deviations used by the innovation consistency test.

EKF2_EVV_NOISE.summary: Measurement noise for vision velocity measurements
EKF2_EVV_NOISE.description: Used to lower bound or replace the uncertainty included in the message

EKF2_EV_CTRL.description: Set bits in the following positions to enable: 0 : Horizontal position fusion 1 : Vertical position fusion 2 : 3D velocity fusion 3 : Yaw
choices: Bitmask: 0: Horizontal position, 1: Vertical position, 2: 3D velocity, 3: Yaw

EKF2_EV_DELAY.summary: Vision Position Estimator delay relative to IMU measurements

EKF2_EV_NOISE_MD.description: If set to 0 (default) the measurement noise is taken from the vision message and the EV noise parameters are used as a lower bound. If set to 1 the observation noise is set from the parameters directly,

EKF2_EV_POS_X.summary: X position of VI sensor focal point in body frame
EKF2_EV_POS_X.description: Forward axis with origin relative to vehicle centre of gravity

EKF2_EV_POS_Y.summary: Y position of VI sensor focal point in body frame
EKF2_EV_POS_Y.description: Forward axis with origin relative to vehicle centre of gravity

EKF2_EV_POS_Z.summary: Z position of VI sensor focal point in body frame
EKF2_EV_POS_Z.description: Forward axis with origin relative to vehicle centre of gravity

EKF2_EV_QMIN.description: External vision will only be started and fused if the quality metric is above this threshold. The quality metric is a completely optional field provided by some VIO systems.

EKF2_FUSE_BETA.description: For reliable wind estimation both sideslip and airspeed fusion (see EKF2_ARSP_THR) should be enabled. Only applies to vehicles in fixed-wing mode or with airspeed fusion active. Note: side slip fusion is currently not supported for tailsitters.

EKF2_GND_EFF_DZ.summary: Baro deadzone range for height fusion
EKF2_GND_EFF_DZ.description: Sets the value of deadzone applied to negative baro innovations. Deadzone is enabled when EKF2_GND_EFF_DZ > 0.

EKF2_GND_MAX_HGT.summary: Height above ground level for ground effect zone
EKF2_GND_MAX_HGT.description: Sets the maximum distance to the ground level where negative baro innovations are expected.

EKF2_GPS_CHECK.description: Each threshold value is defined by the parameter indicated next to the check. Drift and offset checks only run when the vehicle is on ground and stationary.
choices: Bitmask: 0: Sat count (EKF2_REQ_NSATS), 1: PDOP (EKF2_REQ_PDOP), 2: EPH (EKF2_REQ_EPH), 3: EPV (EKF2_REQ_EPV), 4: Speed accuracy (EKF2_REQ_SACC), 5: Horizontal position drift (EKF2_REQ_HDRIFT), 6: Vertical position drift (EKF2_REQ_VDRIFT), 7: Horizontal speed offset (EKF2_REQ_HDRIFT), 8: Vertical speed offset (EKF2_REQ_VDRIFT), 9: Spoofing, 10: GPS fix type (EKF2_REQ_FIX), 11: Jamming

EKF2_GPS_CTRL.description: Set bits in the following positions to enable: 0 : Longitude and latitude fusion 1 : Altitude fusion 2 : 3D velocity fusion 3 : Dual antenna heading fusion
choices: Bitmask: 0: Lon/lat, 1: Altitude, 2: 3D velocity, 3: Dual antenna heading

EKF2_GPS_DELAY.summary: GPS measurement delay relative to IMU measurement
EKF2_GPS_DELAY.description: GPS measurement delay relative to IMU measurement if PPS time correction is not available/enabled (PPS_CAP_ENABLE).

EKF2_GPS_MODE.description: Automatic: reset on fusion timeout if no other source of position is available. Dead-reckoning: reset on fusion timeout if no source of velocity is available.

EKF2_GPS_POS_X.summary: X position of GPS antenna in body frame
EKF2_GPS_POS_X.description: Forward (roll) axis with origin relative to vehicle centre of gravity

EKF2_GPS_POS_Y.summary: Y position of GPS antenna in body frame
EKF2_GPS_POS_Y.description: Right (pitch) axis with origin relative to vehicle centre of gravity

EKF2_GPS_POS_Z.summary: Z position of GPS antenna in body frame
EKF2_GPS_POS_Z.description: Down (yaw) axis with origin relative to vehicle centre of gravity

EKF2_GPS_P_GATE.summary: Gate size for GNSS position fusion
EKF2_GPS_P_GATE.description: Sets the number of standard deviations used by the innovation consistency test.

EKF2_GPS_V_GATE.summary: Gate size for GNSS velocity fusion
EKF2_GPS_V_GATE.description: Sets the number of standard deviations used by the innovation consistency test.

EKF2_GPS_YAW_OFF.summary: Heading/Yaw offset for dual antenna GPS

EKF2_GRAV_NOISE.summary: Accelerometer measurement noise for gravity based observations

EKF2_GSF_TAS.summary: Default value of true airspeed used in EKF-GSF AHRS calculation
EKF2_GSF_TAS.description: If no airspeed measurements are available, the EKF-GSF AHRS calculation will assume this value of true airspeed when compensating for centripetal acceleration during turns. Set to zero to disable centripetal acceleration compensation during fixed wing flight modes.

EKF2_GYR_B_LIM.description: The ekf gyro bias states will be limited to within a range equivalent to +- of this value.

EKF2_GYR_B_NOISE.summary: Process noise for IMU rate gyro bias prediction

EKF2_GYR_NOISE.summary: Rate gyro noise for covariance prediction

EKF2_HDG_GATE.description: Sets the number of standard deviations used by the innovation consistency test.

EKF2_HEAD_NOISE.summary: Measurement noise for magnetic heading fusion

EKF2_HGT_REF.summary: Determines the reference source of height data used by the EKF
EKF2_HGT_REF.description: When multiple height sources are enabled at the same time, the height estimate will always converge towards the reference height source selected by this parameter. The range sensor and vision options should only be used when for operation over a flat surface as the local NED origin will move up and down with ground level. If GPS is set as reference but altitude fusion is disabled in EKF2_GPS_CTRL, the GPS altitude is still used to initiaize the bias of the other height sensors.

choices: Bitmask: 0: Gyro Bias, 1: Accel Bias, 2: Gravity vector fusion

EKF2_IMU_POS_X.summary: X position of IMU in body frame
EKF2_IMU_POS_X.description: Forward axis with origin relative to vehicle centre of gravity

EKF2_IMU_POS_Y.summary: Y position of IMU in body frame
EKF2_IMU_POS_Y.description: Forward axis with origin relative to vehicle centre of gravity

EKF2_IMU_POS_Z.summary: Z position of IMU in body frame
EKF2_IMU_POS_Z.description: Forward axis with origin relative to vehicle centre of gravity

EKF2_MAG_ACCLIM.summary: Horizontal acceleration threshold used for heading observability check
EKF2_MAG_ACCLIM.description: The heading is assumed to be observable when the body acceleration is greater than this parameter when a global position/velocity aiding source is active.

EKF2_MAG_B_NOISE.summary: Process noise for body magnetic field prediction

EKF2_MAG_CHECK.description: Bitmask to set which check is used to decide whether the magnetometer data is valid. If GNSS data is received, the magnetic field is compared to a World Magnetic Model (WMM), otherwise an average value is used. This check is useful to reject occasional hard iron disturbance. Set bits to 1 to enable checks. Checks enabled by the following bit positions 0 : Magnetic field strength. Set tolerance using EKF2_MAG_CHK_STR 1 : Magnetic field inclination. Set tolerance using EKF2_MAG_CHK_INC 2 : Wait for GNSS to find the theoretical strength and inclination using the WMM
choices: Bitmask: 0: Strength (EKF2_MAG_CHK_STR), 1: Inclination (EKF2_MAG_CHK_INC), 2: Wait for WMM

EKF2_MAG_CHK_INC.description: Maximum allowed deviation from the expected magnetic field inclination to pass the check.

EKF2_MAG_CHK_STR.description: Maximum allowed deviation from the expected magnetic field strength to pass the check.

EKF2_MAG_DELAY.summary: Magnetometer measurement delay relative to IMU measurements

EKF2_MAG_E_NOISE.summary: Process noise for earth magnetic field prediction

EKF2_MAG_GATE.summary: Gate size for magnetometer XYZ component fusion
EKF2_MAG_GATE.description: Sets the number of standard deviations used by the innovation consistency test.

EKF2_MAG_TYPE.description: Integer controlling the type of magnetometer fusion used - magnetic heading or 3-component vector. The fusion of magnetometer data as a three component vector enables vehicle body fixed hard iron errors to be learned, but requires a stable earth field. If set to 'Automatic' magnetic heading fusion is used when on-ground and 3-axis magnetic field fusion in-flight. If set to 'Magnetic heading' magnetic heading fusion is used at all times. If set to 'None' the magnetometer will not be used under any circumstance. If no external source of yaw is available, it is possible to use post-takeoff horizontal movement combined with GNSS velocity measurements to align the yaw angle. If set to 'Init' the magnetometer is only used to initalize the heading.

EKF2_MCOEF.summary: Propeller momentum drag coefficient for multi-rotor wind estimation
EKF2_MCOEF.description: This parameter controls the prediction of drag produced by the propellers when flying a multi-copter, which enables estimation of wind drift when enabled by the EKF2_DRAG_CTRL parameter. The drag produced by this effect scales with speed not speed squared and is produced because some of the air velocity normal to the propeller axis of rotation is lost when passing through the rotor disc. This  changes the momentum of the flow which creates a drag reaction force. When comparing un-ducted propellers of the same diameter, the effect is roughly proportional to the area of the propeller blades when viewed side on and changes with propeller selection. Momentum drag is significantly higher for ducted rotors. To account for the drag produced by the body which scales with speed squared, see documentation for the EKF2_BCOEF_X and EKF2_BCOEF_Y parameters. Set this parameter to zero to turn off the momentum drag model for both axis.

EKF2_MIN_RNG.summary: Expected range finder reading when on ground
EKF2_MIN_RNG.description: If the vehicle is on ground, is not moving as determined by the motion test and the range finder is returning invalid or no data, then an assumed range value of EKF2_MIN_RNG will be used by the terrain estimator so that a terrain height estimate is available at the start of flight in situations where the range finder may be inside its minimum measurements distance when on ground.

EKF2_MULTI_IMU.description: Maximum number of IMUs to use for Multi-EKF. Set 0 to disable. Requires SENS_IMU_MODE 0.

EKF2_MULTI_MAG.description: Maximum number of magnetometers to use for Multi-EKF. Set 0 to disable. Requires SENS_MAG_MODE 0.

EKF2_NOAID_NOISE.summary: Measurement noise for non-aiding position hold

EKF2_NOAID_TOUT.description: Maximum lapsed time from last fusion of measurements that constrain velocity drift before the EKF will report the horizontal nav solution as invalid

EKF2_OF_DELAY.summary: Optical flow measurement delay relative to IMU measurements
EKF2_OF_DELAY.description: Assumes measurement is timestamped at trailing edge of integration period

EKF2_OF_GATE.summary: Gate size for optical flow fusion
EKF2_OF_GATE.description: Sets the number of standard deviations used by the innovation consistency test.

EKF2_OF_GYR_SRC.summary: Optical flow angular rate compensation source
EKF2_OF_GYR_SRC.description: Auto: use gyro from optical flow message if available, internal gyro otherwise. Internal: always use internal gyro

EKF2_OF_N_MAX.description: Measurement noise for the optical flow sensor when it's reported quality metric is at the minimum

EKF2_OF_N_MIN.description: Measurement noise for the optical flow sensor when it's reported quality metric is at the maximum

EKF2_OF_POS_X.summary: X position of optical flow focal point in body frame
EKF2_OF_POS_X.description: Forward axis with origin relative to vehicle centre of gravity

EKF2_OF_POS_Y.summary: Y position of optical flow focal point in body frame
EKF2_OF_POS_Y.description: Forward axis with origin relative to vehicle centre of gravity

EKF2_OF_POS_Z.summary: Z position of optical flow focal point in body frame
EKF2_OF_POS_Z.description: Forward axis with origin relative to vehicle centre of gravity

EKF2_OF_QMIN.summary: In air optical flow minimum quality
EKF2_OF_QMIN.description: Optical Flow data will only be used in air if the sensor reports a quality metric >= EKF2_OF_QMIN

EKF2_OF_QMIN_GND.summary: On ground optical flow minimum quality
EKF2_OF_QMIN_GND.description: Optical Flow data will only be used on the ground if the sensor reports a quality metric >= EKF2_OF_QMIN_GND

EKF2_PCOEF_XN.summary: Static pressure position error coefficient for the negative X axis
EKF2_PCOEF_XN.description: This is the ratio of static pressure error to dynamic pressure generated by a negative wind relative velocity along the X body axis. If the baro height estimate rises during backwards flight, then this will be a negative number.

EKF2_PCOEF_XP.summary: Static pressure position error coefficient for the positive X axis
EKF2_PCOEF_XP.description: This is the ratio of static pressure error to dynamic pressure generated by a positive wind relative velocity along the X body axis. If the baro height estimate rises during forward flight, then this will be a negative number.

EKF2_PCOEF_YN.summary: Pressure position error coefficient for the negative Y axis
EKF2_PCOEF_YN.description: This is the ratio of static pressure error to dynamic pressure generated by a wind relative velocity along the negative Y (LH) body axis. If the baro height estimate rises during sideways flight to the left, then this will be a negative number.

EKF2_PCOEF_YP.summary: Pressure position error coefficient for the positive Y axis
EKF2_PCOEF_YP.description: This is the ratio of static pressure error to dynamic pressure generated by a wind relative velocity along the positive Y (RH) body axis. If the baro height estimate rises during sideways flight to the right, then this will be a negative number.

EKF2_PCOEF_Z.summary: Static pressure position error coefficient for the Z axis
EKF2_PCOEF_Z.description: This is the ratio of static pressure error to dynamic pressure generated by a wind relative velocity along the Z body axis.

EKF2_PREDICT_US.description: EKF prediction period in microseconds. This should ideally be an integer multiple of the IMU time delta. Actual filter update will be an integer multiple of IMU update.

EKF2_REQ_FIX.description: Minimum GPS fix type required for GPS usage.

EKF2_REQ_GPS_H.summary: Required GPS health time on startup
EKF2_REQ_GPS_H.description: Minimum continuous period without GPS failure required to mark a healthy GPS status. It can be reduced to speed up initialization, but it's recommended to keep this unchanged for a vehicle.

EKF2_REQ_HDRIFT.summary: Maximum horizontal drift speed to use GPS

EKF2_REQ_NSATS.summary: Required satellite count to use GPS

EKF2_REQ_SACC.summary: Required speed accuracy to use GPS

EKF2_REQ_VDRIFT.summary: Maximum vertical drift speed to use GPS

EKF2_RNG_A_HMAX.summary: Maximum height above ground allowed for conditional range aid mode
EKF2_RNG_A_HMAX.description: If the vehicle absolute altitude exceeds this value then the estimator will not fuse range measurements to estimate its height. This only applies when conditional range aid mode is activated (EKF2_RNG_CTRL = 1).

EKF2_RNG_A_VMAX.summary: Maximum horizontal velocity allowed for conditional range aid mode
EKF2_RNG_A_VMAX.description: If the vehicle horizontal speed exceeds this value then the estimator will not fuse range measurements to estimate its height. This only applies when conditional range aid mode is activated (EKF2_RNG_CTRL = 1).

EKF2_RNG_CTRL.description: WARNING: Range finder measurements are less reliable and can experience unexpected errors. For these reasons, if accurate control of height relative to ground is required, it is recommended to use the MPC_ALT_MODE parameter instead, unless baro errors are severe enough to cause problems with landing and takeoff. If this parameter is enabled then the estimator will make use of the range finder measurements to estimate its height in addition to other height sources (if activated). Range sensor aiding can be enabled (i.e.: always use) or set in "conditional" mode. Conditional mode: This enables the range finder to be used during low speed (< EKF2_RNG_A_VMAX) and low altitude (< EKF2_RNG_A_HMAX) operation, eg takeoff and landing, where baro interference from rotor wash is excessive and can corrupt EKF state estimates. It is intended to be used where a vertical takeoff and landing is performed, and horizontal flight does not occur until above EKF2_RNG_A_HMAX.

EKF2_RNG_DELAY.summary: Range finder measurement delay relative to IMU measurements

EKF2_RNG_FOG.summary: Maximum distance at which the range finder could detect fog (m)
EKF2_RNG_FOG.description: Limit for fog detection. If the range finder measures a distance greater than this value, the measurement is considered to not be blocked by fog or rain. If there's a jump from larger than RNG_FOG to smaller than EKF2_RNG_FOG, the measurement may gets rejected. 0 - disabled

EKF2_RNG_GATE.summary: Gate size for range finder fusion
EKF2_RNG_GATE.description: Sets the number of standard deviations used by the innovation consistency test.

EKF2_RNG_K_GATE.summary: Gate size used for range finder kinematic consistency check
EKF2_RNG_K_GATE.description: To be used, the time derivative of the distance sensor measurements projected on the vertical axis needs to be statistically consistent with the estimated vertical velocity of the drone. Decrease this value to make the filter more robust against range finder faulty data (stuck, reflections, ...). Note: tune the range finder noise parameters (EKF2_RNG_NOISE and EKF2_RNG_SFE) before tuning this gate.

EKF2_RNG_NOISE.summary: Measurement noise for range finder fusion

EKF2_RNG_POS_X.summary: X position of range finder origin in body frame
EKF2_RNG_POS_X.description: Forward axis with origin relative to vehicle centre of gravity

EKF2_RNG_POS_Y.summary: Y position of range finder origin in body frame
EKF2_RNG_POS_Y.description: Forward axis with origin relative to vehicle centre of gravity

EKF2_RNG_POS_Z.summary: Z position of range finder origin in body frame
EKF2_RNG_POS_Z.description: Forward axis with origin relative to vehicle centre of gravity

EKF2_RNG_QLTY_T.description: Minimum duration during which the reported range finder signal quality needs to be non-zero in order to be declared valid (s)

EKF2_RNG_SFE.summary: Range finder range dependent noise scaler
EKF2_RNG_SFE.description: Specifies the increase in range finder noise with range.

EKF2_SEL_ERR_RED.description: EKF2 instances have to be better than the selected by at least this amount before their relative score can be reduced.

EKF2_SEL_IMU_ACC.description: EKF2 selector acceleration error threshold for comparing accelerometers. Acceleration vector differences larger than this will result in accumulated velocity error.

EKF2_SEL_IMU_ANG.description: EKF2 selector maximum accumulated angular error threshold for comparing gyros. Accumulated angular error larger than this will result in the sensor being declared faulty.

EKF2_SEL_IMU_RAT.description: EKF2 selector angular rate error threshold for comparing gyros. Angular rate vector differences larger than this will result in accumulated angular error.

EKF2_SEL_IMU_VEL.description: EKF2 selector maximum accumulated velocity threshold for comparing accelerometers. Accumulated velocity error larger than this will result in the sensor being declared faulty.

EKF2_SYNT_MAG_Z.summary: Enable synthetic magnetometer Z component measurement
EKF2_SYNT_MAG_Z.description: Use for vehicles where the measured body Z magnetic field is subject to strong magnetic interference. For magnetic heading fusion the magnetometer Z measurement will be replaced by a synthetic value calculated using the knowledge of the 3D magnetic field vector at the location of the drone. Therefore, this parameter will only have an effect if the global position of the drone is known. For 3D mag fusion the magnetometer Z measurement will simply be ignored instead of fusing the synthetic value.

EKF2_TAS_GATE.description: Sets the number of standard deviations used by the innovation consistency test.

EKF2_TAU_POS.description: Controls how tightly the output track the EKF states

EKF2_TAU_VEL.summary: Time constant of the velocity output prediction and smoothing filter

EKF2_WIND_NSD.summary: Process noise spectral density for wind velocity prediction
EKF2_WIND_NSD.description: When unaided, the wind estimate uncertainty (1-sigma, in m/s) increases by this amount every second.

EV_TSK_RC_LOSS.description:
Enable/disable event task for RC Loss. When enabled, an alarm tune will be
played via buzzer or ESCs, if supported. The alarm will sound after a disarm,
if the vehicle was previously armed and only if the vehicle had RC signal at
some point. Particularly useful for locating crashed drones without a GPS
sensor.

EV_TSK_STAT_DIS.description:
Enable/disable event task for displaying the vehicle status using arm-mounted
LEDs. When enabled and if the vehicle supports it, LEDs will flash
indicating various vehicle status changes. Currently PX4 has not implemented
any specific status events.
-

FW_MAN_P_MAX.description: Applies to both directions in all manual modes with attitude stabilization but without altitude control

FW_MAN_R_MAX.description: Applies to both directions in all manual modes with attitude stabilization

FW_MAN_YR_MAX.description:
This is the maximally added yaw rate setpoint from the yaw stick in any attitude controlled flight mode.
It is added to the yaw rate setpoint generated by the controller for turn coordination.

FW_PSP_OFF.summary: Pitch setpoint offset (pitch at level flight)
FW_PSP_OFF.description:
An airframe specific offset of the pitch setpoint in degrees, the value is
added to the pitch setpoint and should correspond to the pitch at
typical cruise speed of the airframe.

FW_P_RMAX_NEG.summary: Maximum negative / down pitch rate setpoint

FW_P_RMAX_POS.summary: Maximum positive / up pitch rate setpoint

FW_P_TC.description:
This defines the latency between a pitch step input and the achieved setpoint
(inverse to a P gain). Smaller systems may require smaller values.

FW_R_TC.description:
This defines the latency between a roll step input and the achieved setpoint
(inverse to a P gain). Smaller systems may require smaller values.

FW_WR_I.description:
This gain defines how much control response will result out of a steady
state error. It trims any constant error.

FW_WR_P.description:
This defines how much the wheel steering input will be commanded depending on the
current body angular rate error.

FW_W_EN.description:
Only enabled during automatic runway takeoff and landing.
In all manual modes the wheel is directly controlled with yaw stick.

FW_W_RMAX.description:
This limits the maximum wheel steering rate the controller will output (in degrees per
second).

FW_FLAPS_LND_SCL.description:
Sets a fraction of full flaps during landing.
Also applies to flaperons if enabled in the mixer/allocation.

FW_LND_ABORT.summary: Bit mask to set the automatic landing abort conditions
FW_LND_ABORT.description:
Terrain estimation:
bit 0: Abort if terrain is not found
bit 1: Abort if terrain times out (after a first successful measurement)
The last estimate is always used as ground, whether the last valid measurement or the land waypoint, depending on the
selected abort criteria, until an abort condition is entered. If FW_LND_USETER == 0, these bits are ignored.
TODO: Extend automatic abort conditions
e.g. glide slope tracking error (horizontal and vertical)
choices: Bitmask: 0: Abort if terrain is not found (only applies to mission landings), 1: Abort if terrain times out (after a first successful measurement)

FW_LND_AIRSPD.description:
The calibrated airspeed setpoint during landing.
If set <= 0, landing airspeed = FW_AIRSPD_MIN by default.

FW_LND_ANG.description:
Typically the desired landing slope angle when landing configuration (flaps, airspeed) is enabled.
Set this value within the vehicle's performance limits.

FW_LND_EARLYCFG.description:
Allows to deploy the landing configuration (flaps, landing airspeed, etc.) already in
the loiter-down waypoint before the final approach.
Otherwise is enabled only in the final approach.

FW_LND_FLALT.summary: Landing flare altitude (relative to landing altitude)
FW_LND_FLALT.description: NOTE: max(FW_LND_FLALT, FW_LND_FL_TIME * |z-velocity|) is taken as the flare altitude

FW_LND_FL_SINK.description: TECS will attempt to control the aircraft to this sink rate via pitch angle (throttle killed during flare)

FW_LND_FL_TIME.description:
Multiplied by the descent rate to calculate a dynamic altitude at which
to trigger the flare.
NOTE: max(FW_LND_FLALT, FW_LND_FL_TIME * descent rate) is taken as the flare altitude

FW_LND_NUDGE.description:
Approach angle nudging: shifts the touchdown point laterally while keeping the approach entrance point constant
Approach path nudging: shifts the touchdown point laterally along with the entire approach path
This is useful for manually adjusting the landing point in real time when map or GNSS errors cause an offset from the
desired landing vector. Nudging is done with yaw stick, constrained to FW_LND_TD_OFF (in meters) and the direction is
relative to the vehicle heading (stick deflection to the right = land point moves to the right as seen by the vehicle).

FW_LND_TD_OFF.summary: Maximum lateral position offset for the touchdown point

FW_LND_TD_TIME.description:
This is the time after the start of flaring that we expect the vehicle to touch the runway.
At this time, a 0.5s clamp down ramp will engage, constraining the pitch setpoint to RWTO_PSP.
If enabled, ensure that RWTO_PSP is configured appropriately for full gear contact on ground roll.
Set to -1.0 to disable touchdown clamping. E.g. it may not be desirable to clamp on belly landings.
The touchdown time will be constrained to be greater than or equal to the flare time (FW_LND_FL_TIME).

FW_LND_THRTC_SC.summary: Altitude time constant factor for landing and low-height flight
FW_LND_THRTC_SC.description: The TECS altitude time constant (FW_T_ALT_TC) is multiplied by this value.

FW_LND_USETER.description:
This is critical for detecting when to flare, and should be enabled if possible.
If enabled and no measurement is found within a given timeout, the landing waypoint altitude will be used OR the landing
will be aborted, depending on the criteria set in FW_LND_ABORT.
If disabled, FW_LND_ABORT terrain based criteria are ignored.
choices: 1: Use the terrain estimate to trigger the flare (only)
2: Calculate landing glide slope relative to the terrain estimate

FW_FLAPS_TO_SCL.description:
Sets a fraction of full flaps during take-off.
Also applies to flaperons if enabled in the mixer/allocation.

FW_LAUN_AC_T.description: Launch is detected when acceleration in body forward direction is above FW_LAUN_AC_THLD for FW_LAUN_AC_T seconds.

FW_LAUN_AC_THLD.description: Launch is detected when acceleration in body forward direction is above FW_LAUN_AC_THLD for FW_LAUN_AC_T seconds.

FW_LAUN_CS_LK_DY.description:
Locks control surfaces during pre-launch (armed) and until this time since launch has passed.
Only affects control surfaces that have corresponding flag set, and not active for runway takeoff.
Set to 0 to disable any surface locking after arming.

FW_LAUN_DETCN_ON.description:
Enables automatic launch detection based on measured acceleration. Use for hand- or catapult-launched vehicles.
Not compatible with runway takeoff.

FW_LAUN_MOT_DEL.description: Start the motor(s) this amount of seconds after launch is detected.

FW_TKO_AIRSPD.description:
The calibrated airspeed setpoint during the takeoff climbout.
If set <= 0, FW_AIRSPD_MIN will be set by default.

FW_GPSF_LT.description:
The time the system should do open loop loiter and wait for GPS recovery
before it starts descending. Set to 0 to disable. Roll angle is set to FW_GPSF_R.
Does only apply for fixed-wing vehicles or VTOLs with NAV_FORCE_VT set to 0.

FW_GPSF_R.description: Roll angle in GPS failure loiter mode.

FW_POS_STK_CONF.description: Applies in manual Position and Altitude flight modes.
choices: Bitmask: 0: Alternative stick configuration (height rate on throttle stick, airspeed on pitch stick), 1: Enable airspeed setpoint via sticks in altitude and position flight mode

FW_P_LIM_MAX.description: Applies in any altitude controlled flight mode.

FW_P_LIM_MIN.description: Applies in any altitude controlled flight mode.

FW_R_LIM.description: Applies in any altitude controlled flight mode.

FW_THR_IDLE.description: This is the minimum throttle while on the ground ("landed") in auto modes.

FW_THR_MAX.description:
Applies in any altitude controlled flight mode.
Should be set accordingly to achieve FW_T_CLMB_MAX.

FW_THR_MIN.description:
Applies in any altitude controlled flight mode.
Usually set to 0 but can be increased to prevent the motor from stopping when
descending, which can increase achievable descent rates.

FW_T_CLMB_R_SP.description:
In auto modes: default climb rate output by controller to achieve altitude setpoints.
In manual modes: maximum climb rate setpoint.

FW_T_SINK_R_SP.description:
In auto modes: default sink rate output by controller to achieve altitude setpoints.
In manual modes: maximum sink rate setpoint.

FW_T_SPDWEIGHT.description:
Adjusts the amount of weighting that the pitch control
applies to speed vs height errors.
0 -> control height only
2 -> control speed only (gliders)

FW_WING_HEIGHT.summary: Height (AGL) of the wings when the aircraft is on the ground
FW_WING_HEIGHT.description:
This is used to constrain a minimum altitude below which we keep wings level to avoid wing tip strike. It's safer
to give a slight margin here (> 0m)

FW_WING_SPAN.summary: The aircraft's wing span (length from tip to tip)
FW_WING_SPAN.description: This is used for limiting the roll setpoint near the ground. (if multiple wings, take the longest span)

FW_PN_R_SLEW_MAX.summary: Path navigation roll slew rate limit
FW_PN_R_SLEW_MAX.description:
Maximum change in roll angle setpoint per second.
Applied in all Auto modes, plus manual Position & Altitude modes.

FW_GND_SPD_MIN.description:
The controller will increase the commanded airspeed to maintain
this minimum groundspeed to the next waypoint.

FW_THR_SLEW_MAX.description: Maximum slew rate for the commanded throttle

FW_T_F_ALT_ERR.description:
Minimum altitude error needed to descend with max airspeed and minimal throttle.
A negative value disables fast descend.

FW_T_I_GAIN_PIT.description:
Increase it to trim out speed and height offsets faster,
with the downside of possible overshoots and oscillations.

FW_T_RLL2THR.description:
Is used to compensate for the additional drag created by turning.
Increase this gain if the aircraft initially loses energy in turns
and reduce if the aircraft initially gains energy in turns.

FW_T_SEB_R_FF.summary: Specific total energy balance rate feedforward gain

FW_T_SPD_DEV_STD.description: For the airspeed filter in TECS.

FW_T_SPD_PRC_STD.summary: Process noise standard deviation for the airspeed rate
FW_T_SPD_PRC_STD.description:
This is defining the noise in the airspeed rate for the constant airspeed rate model
of the TECS airspeed filter.

FW_T_SPD_STD.description: For the airspeed filter in TECS.

FW_T_STE_R_TC.summary: Specific total energy rate first order filter time constant
FW_T_STE_R_TC.description: This filter is applied to the specific total energy rate used for throttle damping.

FW_T_THR_DAMPING.description: This is the damping gain for the throttle demand loop.

FW_T_THR_INTEG.description:
Increase it to trim out speed and height offsets faster,
with the downside of possible overshoots and oscillations.

FW_T_THR_LOW_HGT.summary: Low-height threshold for tighter altitude tracking
FW_T_THR_LOW_HGT.description:
Height above ground threshold below which tighter altitude
tracking gets enabled (see FW_LND_THRTC_SC). Below this height, TECS smoothly
(1 sec / sec) transitions the altitude tracking time constant from FW_T_ALT_TC
to FW_LND_THRTC_SC*FW_T_ALT_TC.
-1 to disable.

FW_T_VERT_ACC.description:
This is the maximum vertical acceleration
either up or down that the controller will use to correct speed
or height errors.

FW_WIND_ARSP_SC.description:
Multiplying this factor with the current absolute wind estimate gives the airspeed offset
added to the minimum airspeed setpoint limit. This helps to make the
system more robust against disturbances (turbulence) in high wind.

NPFG_DAMPING.description: Damping ratio of NPFG control law.

NPFG_LB_PERIOD.summary: Enable automatic lower bound on the NPFG period
NPFG_LB_PERIOD.description:
Avoids limit cycling from a too aggressively tuned period/damping combination.
If false, also disables upper bound NPFG_PERIOD_UB.

NPFG_PERIOD_SF.description:
Multiplied by period for conservative minimum period bounding (when period lower
bounding is enabled). 1.0 bounds at marginal stability.

NPFG_ROLL_TC.description:
Time constant of roll controller command / response, modeled as first order delay.
Used to determine lower period bound. Setting zero disables automatic period bounding.

NPFG_SW_DST_MLT.description:
Multiplied by the track error boundary to determine when the aircraft switches
to the next waypoint and/or path segment. Should be less than 1.

NPFG_UB_PERIOD.summary: Enable automatic upper bound on the NPFG period
NPFG_UB_PERIOD.description: Adapts period to maintain track keeping in variable winds and path curvature.

FW_AIRSPD_FLP_SC.description: Factor applied to the minimum and stall airspeed when flaps are fully deployed.

FW_AIRSPD_MAX.description: The maximal airspeed (calibrated airspeed) the user is able to command.

FW_AIRSPD_MIN.description:
The minimal airspeed (calibrated airspeed) the user is able to command.
Further, if the airspeed falls below this value, the TECS controller will try to
increase airspeed more aggressively.
Has to be set according to the vehicle's stall speed (which should be set in FW_AIRSPD_STALL),
with some margin between the stall speed and minimum airspeed.
This value corresponds to the desired minimum speed with the default load factor (level flight, default weight),
and is automatically adpated to the current load factor (calculated from roll setpoint and WEIGHT_GROSS/WEIGHT_BASE).

FW_AIRSPD_STALL.description:
The stall airspeed (calibrated airspeed) of the vehicle.
It is used for airspeed sensor failure detection and for the control
surface scaling airspeed limits.

FW_AIRSPD_TRIM.description:
The trim CAS (calibrated airspeed) of the vehicle. If an airspeed controller is active,
this is the default airspeed setpoint that the controller will try to achieve.
This value corresponds to the trim airspeed with the default load factor (level flight, default weight).

FW_SERVICE_CEIL.description:
Altitude in standard atmosphere at which the vehicle in normal configuration (WEIGHT_BASE) is still able to achieve a maximum climb rate of
0.5m/s at maximum throttle (FW_THR_MAX). Used to compensate for air density in FW_T_CLMB_MAX.
Set negative to disable.

FW_THR_ASPD_MAX.description:
Required throttle (at sea level, standard atmosphere) for level flight at maximum airspeed FW_AIRSPD_MAX
Set to 0 to disable mapping of airspeed to trim throttle.

FW_THR_ASPD_MIN.description:
Required throttle (at sea level, standard atmosphere) for level flight at minimum airspeed FW_AIRSPD_MIN
Set to 0 to disable mapping of airspeed to trim throttle below FW_AIRSPD_TRIM.

FW_THR_TRIM.description: Required throttle (at sea level, standard atmosphere) for level flight at FW_AIRSPD_TRIM

FW_T_CLMB_MAX.description:
This is the maximum calibrated climb rate that the aircraft can achieve with
the throttle set to FW_THR_MAX and the airspeed set to the
trim value. For electric aircraft make sure this number can be
achieved towards the end of flight when the battery voltage has reduced.

FW_T_SINK_MIN.description:
This is the minimum calibrated sink rate of the aircraft with the throttle
set to THR_MIN and flown at the same airspeed as used
to measure FW_T_CLMB_MAX.

WEIGHT_BASE.description:
This is the weight of the vehicle at which it's performance limits were derived. A zero or negative value
disables trim throttle and minimum airspeed compensation based on weight.

WEIGHT_GROSS.description:
This is the actual weight of the vehicle at any time. This value will differ from WEIGHT_BASE in case weight was added
or removed from the base weight. Examples are the addition of payloads or larger batteries. A zero or negative value
disables trim throttle and minimum airspeed compensation based on weight.

FW_ACRO_X_MAX.summary: Acro body roll max rate setpoint

FW_ACRO_YAW_EN.summary: Enable yaw rate controller in Acro
FW_ACRO_YAW_EN.description:
If this parameter is set to 1, the yaw rate controller is enabled in Fixed-wing Acro mode.
Otherwise the pilot commands directly the yaw actuator.
It is disabled by default because an active yaw rate controller will fight against the
natural turn coordination of the plane.

FW_ACRO_Y_MAX.summary: Acro body pitch max rate setpoint

FW_ACRO_Z_MAX.summary: Acro body yaw max rate setpoint

FW_ARSP_SCALE_EN.description:
This enables a logic that automatically adjusts the output of the rate controller to take
into account the real torque produced by an aerodynamic control surface given
the current deviation from the trim airspeed (FW_AIRSPD_TRIM).
Enable when using aerodynamic control surfaces (e.g.: plane)
Disable when using rotor wings (e.g.: autogyro)

FW_BAT_SCALE_EN.summary: Enable throttle scale by battery level
FW_BAT_SCALE_EN.description:
This compensates for voltage drop of the battery over time by attempting to
normalize performance across the operating range of the battery.

FW_DTRIM_P_VMAX.summary: Pitch trim increment at maximum airspeed
FW_DTRIM_P_VMAX.description: This increment is added to TRIM_PITCH when airspeed is FW_AIRSPD_MAX.

FW_DTRIM_P_VMIN.summary: Pitch trim increment at minimum airspeed
FW_DTRIM_P_VMIN.description: This increment is added to TRIM_PITCH when airspeed is FW_AIRSPD_MIN.

FW_DTRIM_R_VMAX.summary: Roll trim increment at maximum airspeed
FW_DTRIM_R_VMAX.description: This increment is added to TRIM_ROLL when airspeed is FW_AIRSPD_MAX.

FW_DTRIM_R_VMIN.summary: Roll trim increment at minimum airspeed
FW_DTRIM_R_VMIN.description: This increment is added to TRIM_ROLL when airspeed is FW_AIRSPD_MIN.

FW_DTRIM_Y_VMAX.summary: Yaw trim increment at maximum airspeed
FW_DTRIM_Y_VMAX.description: This increment is added to TRIM_YAW when airspeed is FW_AIRSPD_MAX.

FW_DTRIM_Y_VMIN.summary: Yaw trim increment at minimum airspeed
FW_DTRIM_Y_VMIN.description: This increment is added to TRIM_YAW when airspeed is FW_AIRSPD_MIN.

FW_GC_GAIN_MIN.description: The range of the compression gain is between this parameter and 1.0

FW_MAN_P_SC.description:
Scale factor applied to the desired pitch actuator command in full manual mode. This parameter allows
to adjust the throws of the control surfaces.

FW_MAN_R_SC.description:
Scale factor applied to the desired roll actuator command in full manual mode. This parameter allows
to adjust the throws of the control surfaces.

FW_MAN_Y_SC.description:
Scale factor applied to the desired yaw actuator command in full manual mode. This parameter allows
to adjust the throws of the control surfaces.

FW_PR_FF.description: Direct feed forward from rate setpoint to control surface output

FW_RLL_TO_YAW_FF.summary: Roll control to yaw control feedforward gain
FW_RLL_TO_YAW_FF.description:
This gain can be used to counteract the "adverse yaw" effect for fixed wings.
When the plane enters a roll it will tend to yaw the nose out of the turn.
This gain enables the use of a yaw actuator to counteract this effect.

FW_RR_FF.description: Direct feed forward from rate setpoint to control surface output.

FW_SPOILERS_MAN.description: Chose source for manual setting of spoilers in manual flight modes.

FW_USE_AIRSPD.description:
If set to 1, the airspeed measurement data, if valid, is used in the following controllers:
- Rate controller: output scaling
- Attitude controller: coordinated turn controller
- Position controller: airspeed setpoint tracking, takeoff logic
- VTOL: transition logic

FW_YR_FF.description: Direct feed forward from rate setpoint to control surface output

FD_ACT_EN.description:
If enabled, failure detector will verify that for motors, a minimum amount of ESC current per throttle
level is being consumed.
Otherwise this indicates an motor failure.

FD_ACT_MOT_C2T.description:
Determines the slope between expected steady state current and linearized, normalized thrust command.
E.g. FD_ACT_MOT_C2T A represents the expected steady state current at 100%.
FD_ACT_LOW_OFF and FD_ACT_HIGH_OFF offset the threshold from that slope.

FD_ACT_MOT_THR.description:
Failure detection per motor only triggers above this thrust value.
Set to 1 to disable the detection.

FD_ACT_MOT_TOUT.description: Motor failure only triggers after current thresholds are exceeded for this time.

FD_ESCS_EN.summary: Enable checks on ESCs that report their arming state
FD_ESCS_EN.description:
If enabled, failure detector will verify that all the ESCs have successfully armed when the vehicle has transitioned to the armed state.
Timeout for receiving an acknowledgement from the ESCs is 0.3s, if no feedback is received the failure detector will auto disarm the vehicle.

FD_EXT_ATS_EN.summary: Enable PWM input on for engaging failsafe from an external automatic trigger system (ATS)
FD_EXT_ATS_EN.description:
Enabled on either AUX5 or MAIN5 depending on board.
External ATS is required by ASTM F3322-18.

FD_EXT_ATS_TRIG.summary: The PWM threshold from external automatic trigger system for engaging failsafe
FD_EXT_ATS_TRIG.description: External ATS is required by ASTM F3322-18.

FD_FAIL_P.description:
Maximum pitch angle before FailureDetector triggers the attitude_failure flag.
The flag triggers flight termination (if @CBRK_FLIGHTTERM = 0),
which sets outputs to their failsafe values.
On takeoff the flag triggers lockdown (irrespective of @CBRK_FLIGHTTERM),
which disarms motors but does not set outputs to failsafe values.
Setting this parameter to 0 disables the check

FD_FAIL_P_TTRI.description: Seconds (decimal) that pitch has to exceed FD_FAIL_P before being considered as a failure.

FD_FAIL_R.description:
Maximum roll angle before FailureDetector triggers the attitude_failure flag.
The flag triggers flight termination (if @CBRK_FLIGHTTERM = 0),
which sets outputs to their failsafe values.
On takeoff the flag triggers lockdown (irrespective of @CBRK_FLIGHTTERM),
which disarms motors but does not set outputs to failsafe values.
Setting this parameter to 0 disables the check

FD_FAIL_R_TTRI.description: Seconds (decimal) that roll has to exceed FD_FAIL_R before being considered as a failure.

FD_IMB_PROP_THR.description:
Value at which the imbalanced propeller metric (based on horizontal and
vertical acceleration variance) triggers a failure
Setting this value to 0 disables the feature.

FLW_TGT_ALT_M.description:
Maintain altitude or track target's altitude. When maintaining the altitude,
the drone can crash into terrain when the target moves uphill. When tracking
the target's altitude, the follow altitude FLW_TGT_HT should be high enough
to prevent terrain collisions due to GPS inaccuracies of the target.
choices: 0: 2D Tracking: Maintain constant altitude relative to home and track XY position only
1: 2D + Terrain: Maintain constant altitude relative to terrain below and track XY position
2: 3D Tracking: Track target's altitude (be aware that GPS altitude bias usually makes this useless)

FLW_TGT_DST.description: The distance in meters to follow the target at

FLW_TGT_FA.description:
Angle to follow the target from. 0.0 Equals straight in front of the target's
course (direction of motion) and the angle increases in clockwise direction,
meaning Right-side would be 90.0 degrees while Left-side is -90.0 degrees
Note: When the user force sets the angle out of the min/max range, it will be
wrapped (e.g. 480 -> 120) in the range to gracefully handle the out of range.

FLW_TGT_MAX_VEL.summary: Maximum tangential velocity setting for generating the follow orbit trajectory
FLW_TGT_MAX_VEL.description:
This is the maximum tangential velocity the drone will circle around the target whenever
an orbit angle setpoint changes. Higher value means more aggressive follow behavior.

FLW_TGT_RS.summary: Responsiveness to target movement in Target Estimator
FLW_TGT_RS.description: lower values increase the responsiveness to changing position, but also ignore less noise

GPS_1_GNSS.summary: GNSS Systems for Primary GPS (integer bitmask)
GPS_1_GNSS.description:
This integer bitmask controls the set of GNSS systems used by the receiver. Check your
receiver's documentation on how many systems are supported to be used in parallel.
Currently this functionality is just implemented for u-blox receivers.
When no bits are set, the receiver's default configuration should be used.
Set bits true to enable:
0 : Use GPS (with QZSS)
1 : Use SBAS (multiple GPS augmentation systems)
2 : Use Galileo
3 : Use BeiDou
4 : Use GLONASS
5 : Use NAVIC
choices: Bitmask: 0: GPS (with QZSS), 1: SBAS, 2: Galileo, 3: BeiDou, 4: GLONASS, 5: NAVIC

GPS_1_PROTOCOL.description:
Select the GPS protocol over serial.
Auto-detection will probe all protocols, and thus is a bit slower.

GPS_2_PROTOCOL.description:

GPS_CFG_WIPE.summary: Wipes the flash config of UBX modules
GPS_CFG_WIPE.description:
Some UBX modules have a FLASH that allows to store persistent configuration that will be loaded on start.
PX4 does override all configuration parameters it needs in RAM, which takes precedence over the values in FLASH.
However, configuration parameters that are not overriden by PX4 can still cause unexpected problems during flight.
To avoid these kind of problems a clean config can be reached by wiping the FLASH on boot.
Note: Currently only supported on UBX.

GPS_DUMP_COMM.description:
If this is set to 1, all GPS communication data will be published via uORB,
and written to the log file as gps_dump message.
If this is set to 2, the main GPS is configured to output RTCM data,
which is then logged as gps_dump and can be used for PPK.

GPS_SAT_INFO.description:
Enable publication of satellite info (ORB_ID(satellite_info)) if possible.
Not available on MTK.

GPS_UBX_BAUD2.description:
Select a baudrate for the F9P's UART2 port.
In GPS_UBX_MODE 1, 2, and 3, the F9P's UART2 port is configured to send/receive RTCM corrections.
Set this to 57600 if you want to attach a telemetry radio on UART2.

choices: Bitmask: 0: Enable I2C input protocol UBX, 1: Enable I2C input protocol NMEA, 2: Enable I2C input protocol RTCM3X, 3: Enable I2C output protocol UBX, 4: Enable I2C output protocol NMEA, 5: Enable I2C output protocol RTCM3X

GPS_UBX_DGNSS_TO.description: When set to 0 (default), default DGNSS timeout set by u-blox will be used.

GPS_UBX_DYNMODEL.description:
u-blox receivers support different dynamic platform models to adjust the navigation engine to
the expected application environment.

GPS_UBX_JAM_DET.summary: u-blox GPS jamming detection high sensitivity mode
GPS_UBX_JAM_DET.description:
Enables or disables the high sensitivity mode for the u-blox jamming detection
(CFG-SEC-JAMDET_SENSITIVITY_HI). When enabled, the receiver uses a
more sensitive algorithm to detect jamming. Disabling this may reduce false
positives in electrically noisy environments.

GPS_UBX_MIN_CNO.summary: u-blox GPS minimum satellite signal level for navigation
GPS_UBX_MIN_CNO.description: When set to 0 (default), default minimum satellite signal level set by u-blox wll be used.

GPS_UBX_MIN_ELEV.summary: u-blox GPS minimum elevation for a GNSS satellite to be used in navigation
GPS_UBX_MIN_ELEV.description: When set to 0 (default), default minimum elevation set by u-blox will be used.

GPS_UBX_MODE.description:
Select the u-blox configuration setup. Most setups will use the default, including RTK and
dual GPS without heading.
If rover has RTCM corrections from a static base (or other static correction source) coming in on UART2, then select Mode 5.
The Heading mode requires 2 F9P devices to be attached. The main GPS will act as rover and output
heading information, whereas the secondary will act as moving base.
Modes 1 and 2 require each F9P UART1 to be connected to the Autopilot. In addition, UART2 on the
F9P units are connected to each other.
Modes 3 and 4 only require UART1 on each F9P connected to the Autopilot or Can Node. UART RX DMA is required.
RTK is still possible with this setup.
Mode 6 is intended for use with a ground control station (not necessarily an RTK correction base).
choices: 1: Heading (Rover With Moving Base UART1 Connected To Autopilot, UART2 Connected To Moving Base)
2: Moving Base (UART1 Connected To Autopilot, UART2 Connected To Rover)
3: Heading (Rover With Moving Base UART1 Connected to Autopilot Or Can Node At 921600)
4: Moving Base (Moving Base UART1 Connected to Autopilot Or Can Node At 921600)
5: Rover with Static Base on UART2 (similar to Default, except coming in on UART2)

GPS_UBX_PPK.summary: Enable MSM7 message output for PPK workflow

GPS_UBX_RATE.description:
Configure the output rate of u-blox GPS receivers (protocol v27+).
When set to 0, automatic rate selection is used based on the receiver model.
Default rates: M9N=8Hz, F9P L1L2=5Hz, F9P L1L5=5Hz, Others=10Hz.
Note: Higher rates reduce satellite count (e.g., >8Hz limits to 16 SVs on M9N).
Max rates vary by model and RTK mode: F9P L1L2=5-7Hz, F9P L1L5=7-8Hz, X20=25Hz.
High rates at 115200 baud may cause dropouts.

GPS_YAW_OFFSET.summary: Heading/Yaw offset for dual antenna GPS
GPS_YAW_OFFSET.description:
Heading offset angle for dual antenna GPS setups that support heading estimation.
Set this to 0 if the antennas are parallel to the forward-facing direction
of the vehicle and the rover (or Unicore primary) antenna is in front.
The offset angle increases clockwise.
Set this to 90 if the rover (or Unicore primary, or Septentrio Mosaic Aux)
antenna is placed on the right side of the vehicle and the moving base
antenna is on the left side.
(Note: the Unicore primary antenna is the one connected on the right as seen
from the top).

GF_ACTION.description:
Note: Setting this value to 4 enables flight termination,
which will kill the vehicle on violation of the fence.

GF_MAX_HOR_DIST.description:
Maximum horizontal distance in meters the vehicle can be from Home before triggering a geofence action.
Disabled if 0.

GF_MAX_VER_DIST.description:
Maximum vertical distance in meters the vehicle can be from Home before triggering a geofence action.
Disabled if 0.

GF_PREDICT.description:
WARNING: This experimental feature may cause flyaways. Use at your own risk.
Predict the motion of the vehicle and trigger the breach if it is determined that the current trajectory
would result in a breach happening before the vehicle can make evasive maneuvers.
The vehicle is then re-routed to a safe hold position (stop for multirotor, loiter for fixed wing).

GF_SOURCE.description:
Select which position source should be used. Selecting GPS instead of global position makes sure that there is
no dependence on the position estimator
0 = global position, 1 = GPS

CA_AIRFRAME.description:
Defines which mixer implementation to use.
Some are generic, while others are specifically fit to a certain vehicle with a fixed set of actuators.
'Custom' should only be used if noting else can be used.

CA_CS_LAUN_LK.description: If actuator launch lock is enabled, this surface is kept at the disarmed value.
choices: Bitmask: 0: Control Surface 1, 1: Control Surface 2, 2: Control Surface 3, 3: Control Surface 4, 4: Control Surface 5, 5: Control Surface 6, 6: Control Surface 7, 7: Control Surface 8

CA_FAILURE_MODE.description:
This is used to specify how to handle motor failures
reported by failure detector.
choices: 1: Remove first failed motor from effectiveness

CA_HELI_PITCH_C0.description:
Defines the collective pitch at the interval position 0 for a given thrust setpoint.
Use negative values if the swash plate needs to move down to provide upwards thrust.

CA_HELI_PITCH_C1.description:
Defines the collective pitch at the interval position 1 for a given thrust setpoint.
Use negative values if the swash plate needs to move down to provide upwards thrust.

CA_HELI_PITCH_C2.description:
Defines the collective pitch at the interval position 2 for a given thrust setpoint.
Use negative values if the swash plate needs to move down to provide upwards thrust.

CA_HELI_PITCH_C3.description:
Defines the collective pitch at the interval position 3 for a given thrust setpoint.
Use negative values if the swash plate needs to move down to provide upwards thrust.

CA_HELI_PITCH_C4.description:
Defines the collective pitch at the interval position 4 for a given thrust setpoint.
Use negative values if the swash plate needs to move down to provide upwards thrust.

CA_HELI_RPM_I.description: Same definition as the proportional gain but for integral.

CA_HELI_RPM_P.description:
Ratio between rpm error devided by 1000 to how much normalized output gets added to correct for it.
motor_command = throttle_curve + CA_HELI_RPM_P * (rpm_setpoint - rpm_measurement) / 1000

CA_HELI_RPM_SP.description: Requires rpm feedback for the controller.

CA_HELI_THR_C0.description: Defines the output throttle at the interval position 0.

CA_HELI_THR_C1.description: Defines the output throttle at the interval position 1.

CA_HELI_THR_C2.description: Defines the output throttle at the interval position 2.

CA_HELI_THR_C3.description: Defines the output throttle at the interval position 3.

CA_HELI_THR_C4.description: Defines the output throttle at the interval position 4.

CA_HELI_YAW_CCW.description:
Default configuration is for a clockwise turning main rotor and
positive thrust of the tail rotor is expected to rotate the vehicle clockwise.
Set this parameter to true if the tail rotor provides thrust in counter-clockwise direction
which is mostly the case when the main rotor turns counter-clockwise.

CA_HELI_YAW_CP_O.summary: Offset for yaw compensation based on collective pitch
CA_HELI_YAW_CP_O.description:
This allows to specify which collective pitch command results in the least amount of rotor drag.
This is used to increase the accuracy of the yaw drag torque compensation based on collective pitch
by aligning the lowest rotor drag with zero compensation.
For symmetric profile blades this is the command that results in exactly 0° collective blade angle.
For lift profile blades this is typically a command resulting in slightly negative collective blade angle.
tail_output += CA_HELI_YAW_CP_S * abs(collective_pitch - CA_HELI_YAW_CP_O)

CA_HELI_YAW_CP_S.summary: Scale for yaw compensation based on collective pitch
CA_HELI_YAW_CP_S.description:
This allows to add a proportional factor of the collective pitch command to the yaw command.
A negative value is needed when positive thrust of the tail rotor rotates the vehicle opposite to the main rotor turn direction.
tail_output += CA_HELI_YAW_CP_S * abs(collective_pitch - CA_HELI_YAW_CP_O)

CA_HELI_YAW_TH_S.summary: Scale for yaw compensation based on throttle
CA_HELI_YAW_TH_S.description:
This allows to add a proportional factor of the throttle command to the yaw command.
A negative value is needed when positive thrust of the tail rotor rotates the vehicle opposite to the main rotor turn direction.
tail_output += CA_HELI_YAW_TH_S * throttle

CA_ICE_PERIOD.description:
Ice shedding prevents ice buildup in VTOL aircraft motors by periodically spinning inactive rotors.
When enabled (period > 0), every cycle lasts for the defined period and includes a 2-second spin at 0.01 motor output.
If period <= 0, the feature is disabled.

CA_MAX_SVO_THROW.summary: Throw angle of swashplate servo at maximum commands for linearization
CA_MAX_SVO_THROW.description:
Used to linearize mechanical output of swashplate servos to avoid axis coupling and binding with 4 servo redundancy.
This requires a symmetric setup where the servo horn is exactly centered with a 0 command.
Setting to zero disables feature.

CA_METHOD.description:
Selects the algorithm and desaturation method.
If set to Automatic, the selection is based on the airframe (CA_AIRFRAME).

HTE_ACC_GATE.description:
Sets the number of standard deviations used
by the innovation consistency test.

HTE_HT_ERR_INIT.description:
Sets the number of standard deviations used
by the innovation consistency test.

HTE_HT_NOISE.description:
Reduce to make the hover thrust estimate
more stable, increase if the real hover thrust
is expected to change quickly over time.

HTE_THR_RANGE.description:
Defines the range of the hover thrust estimate around MPC_THR_HOVER.
A value of 0.2 with MPC_THR_HOVER at 0.5 results in a range of [0.3, 0.7].
Set to a large value if the vehicle operates in varying physical conditions that
affect the required hover thrust strongly (e.g. differently sized payloads).

HTE_VXY_THR.summary: Horizontal velocity threshold for sensitivity reduction
HTE_VXY_THR.description:
Above this speed, the measurement noise is linearly increased
to reduce the sensitivity of the estimator from biased measurement.
Set to a low value on vehicles with large lifting surfaces.

HTE_VZ_THR.summary: Vertical velocity threshold for sensitivity reduction
HTE_VZ_THR.description:
Above this speed, the measurement noise is linearly increased
to reduce the sensitivity of the estimator from biased measurement.
Set to a low value on vehicles affected by air drag when climbing or descending.

Variance of acceleration measurement used for landing target position prediction.
Higher values results in tighter following of the measurements and more lenient outlier rejection

LTEST_MEAS_UNC.description:
Variance of the landing target measurement from the driver.
Higher values result in less aggressive following of the measurement and a smoother output as well as fewer rejected measurements.

LTEST_MODE.description:
Configure the mode of the landing target. Depending on the mode, the landing target observations are used differently to aid position estimation.
Mode Moving:     The landing target may be moving around while in the field of view of the vehicle. Landing target measurements are not used to aid positioning.
Mode Stationary: The landing target is stationary. Measured velocity w.r.t. the landing target is used to aid velocity estimation.

MAV_0_BROADCAST.summary: Broadcast heartbeats on local network for MAVLink instance 0
MAV_0_BROADCAST.description:
This allows a ground control station to automatically find the drone
on the local network.

MAV_0_FLOW_CTRL.summary: Enable serial flow control for instance 0
MAV_0_FLOW_CTRL.description:
This is used to force flow control on or off for the the mavlink
instance. By default it is auto detected. Use when auto detection fails.

MAV_0_FORWARD.summary: Enable MAVLink Message forwarding for instance 0
MAV_0_FORWARD.description:
If enabled, forward incoming MAVLink messages to other MAVLink ports if the
message is either broadcast or the target is not the autopilot.
This allows for example a GCS to talk to a camera that is connected to the
autopilot via MAVLink (on a different link than the GCS).

MAV_0_HL_FREQ.summary: Configures the frequency of HIGH_LATENCY2 stream for instance 0
MAV_0_HL_FREQ.description:
Positive real value that configures the transmission frequency of the
HIGH_LATENCY2 stream for instance 0, configured in iridium mode.
This parameter has no effect if the instance mode is different from iridium.

MAV_0_MODE.description:
The MAVLink Mode defines the set of streamed messages (for example the
vehicle's attitude) and their sending rates.

MAV_0_RADIO_CTL.summary: Enable software throttling of mavlink on instance 0
MAV_0_RADIO_CTL.description:
If enabled, MAVLink messages will be throttled according to
`txbuf` field reported by radio_status.
Requires a radio to send the mavlink message RADIO_STATUS.

MAV_0_RATE.summary: Maximum MAVLink sending rate for instance 0
MAV_0_RATE.description:
Configure the maximum sending rate for the MAVLink streams in Bytes/sec.
If the configured streams exceed the maximum rate, the sending rate of
each stream is automatically decreased.
If this is set to 0 a value of half of the theoretical maximum bandwidth is used.
This corresponds to baudrate/20 Bytes/s (baudrate/10 = maximum data rate on
8N1-configured links).

MAV_0_REMOTE_PRT.description:
If ethernet enabled and selected as configuration for MAVLink instance 0,
selected remote port will be set and used in MAVLink instance 0.

MAV_0_UDP_PRT.description:
If ethernet enabled and selected as configuration for MAVLink instance 0,
selected udp port will be set and used in MAVLink instance 0.

MAV_1_BROADCAST.summary: Broadcast heartbeats on local network for MAVLink instance 1
MAV_1_BROADCAST.description:
This allows a ground control station to automatically find the drone
on the local network.

MAV_1_FLOW_CTRL.summary: Enable serial flow control for instance 1
MAV_1_FLOW_CTRL.description:
This is used to force flow control on or off for the the mavlink
instance. By default it is auto detected. Use when auto detection fails.

MAV_1_FORWARD.summary: Enable MAVLink Message forwarding for instance 1
MAV_1_FORWARD.description:
If enabled, forward incoming MAVLink messages to other MAVLink ports if the
message is either broadcast or the target is not the autopilot.
This allows for example a GCS to talk to a camera that is connected to the
autopilot via MAVLink (on a different link than the GCS).

MAV_1_HL_FREQ.summary: Configures the frequency of HIGH_LATENCY2 stream for instance 1
MAV_1_HL_FREQ.description:
