HIGH_LATENCY2 stream for instance 1, configured in iridium mode.
This parameter has no effect if the instance mode is different from iridium.

MAV_1_MODE.description:
The MAVLink Mode defines the set of streamed messages (for example the
vehicle's attitude) and their sending rates.

MAV_1_RADIO_CTL.summary: Enable software throttling of mavlink on instance 1
MAV_1_RADIO_CTL.description:
If enabled, MAVLink messages will be throttled according to
`txbuf` field reported by radio_status.
Requires a radio to send the mavlink message RADIO_STATUS.

MAV_1_RATE.summary: Maximum MAVLink sending rate for instance 1
MAV_1_RATE.description:
Configure the maximum sending rate for the MAVLink streams in Bytes/sec.
If the configured streams exceed the maximum rate, the sending rate of
each stream is automatically decreased.
If this is set to 0 a value of half of the theoretical maximum bandwidth is used.
This corresponds to baudrate/20 Bytes/s (baudrate/10 = maximum data rate on
8N1-configured links).

MAV_1_REMOTE_PRT.description:
If ethernet enabled and selected as configuration for MAVLink instance 1,
selected remote port will be set and used in MAVLink instance 1.

MAV_1_UDP_PRT.description:
If ethernet enabled and selected as configuration for MAVLink instance 1,
selected udp port will be set and used in MAVLink instance 1.

MAV_2_BROADCAST.summary: Broadcast heartbeats on local network for MAVLink instance 2
MAV_2_BROADCAST.description:
This allows a ground control station to automatically find the drone
on the local network.

MAV_2_FLOW_CTRL.summary: Enable serial flow control for instance 2
MAV_2_FLOW_CTRL.description:
This is used to force flow control on or off for the the mavlink
instance. By default it is auto detected. Use when auto detection fails.

MAV_2_FORWARD.summary: Enable MAVLink Message forwarding for instance 2
MAV_2_FORWARD.description:
If enabled, forward incoming MAVLink messages to other MAVLink ports if the
message is either broadcast or the target is not the autopilot.
This allows for example a GCS to talk to a camera that is connected to the
autopilot via MAVLink (on a different link than the GCS).

MAV_2_HL_FREQ.summary: Configures the frequency of HIGH_LATENCY2 stream for instance 2
MAV_2_HL_FREQ.description:
Positive real value that configures the transmission frequency of the
HIGH_LATENCY2 stream for instance 2, configured in iridium mode.
This parameter has no effect if the instance mode is different from iridium.

MAV_2_MODE.description:
The MAVLink Mode defines the set of streamed messages (for example the
vehicle's attitude) and their sending rates.

MAV_2_RADIO_CTL.summary: Enable software throttling of mavlink on instance 2
MAV_2_RADIO_CTL.description:
If enabled, MAVLink messages will be throttled according to
`txbuf` field reported by radio_status.
Requires a radio to send the mavlink message RADIO_STATUS.

MAV_2_RATE.summary: Maximum MAVLink sending rate for instance 2
MAV_2_RATE.description:
Configure the maximum sending rate for the MAVLink streams in Bytes/sec.
If the configured streams exceed the maximum rate, the sending rate of
each stream is automatically decreased.
If this is set to 0 a value of half of the theoretical maximum bandwidth is used.
This corresponds to baudrate/20 Bytes/s (baudrate/10 = maximum data rate on
8N1-configured links).

MAV_2_REMOTE_PRT.description:
If ethernet enabled and selected as configuration for MAVLink instance 2,
selected remote port will be set and used in MAVLink instance 2.

MAV_2_UDP_PRT.description:
If ethernet enabled and selected as configuration for MAVLink instance 2,
selected udp port will be set and used in MAVLink instance 2.

MAV_FWDEXTSP.description:
If set to 1 incoming external setpoint messages will be directly forwarded
to the controllers if in offboard control mode

MAV_HASH_CHK_EN.description:
Disabling the parameter hash check functionality will make the mavlink instance
stream parameters continuously.

MAV_HB_FORW_EN.description:
The mavlink heartbeat message will not be forwarded if this parameter is set to 'disabled'.
The main reason for disabling heartbeats to be forwarded is because they confuse dronekit.

choices: 1: Version 1 with auto-upgrade to v2 if detected

MAV_RADIO_TOUT.summary: Timeout in seconds for the RADIO_STATUS reports coming in
MAV_RADIO_TOUT.description:
If the connected radio stops reporting RADIO_STATUS for a certain time,
a warning is triggered and, if MAV_X_RADIO_CTL is enabled, the software-flow
control is reset.

MAV_SIK_RADIO_ID.description:
When non-zero the MAVLink app will attempt to configure the
SiK radio to this ID and re-set the parameter to 0. If the value
is negative it will reset the complete radio config to
factory defaults. Only applies if this mavlink instance is going through a SiK radio

MAV_S_MODE.summary: MAVLink Mode for SOM to FMU communication channel
MAV_S_MODE.description:
The MAVLink Mode defines the set of streamed messages (for example the
vehicle's attitude) and their sending rates.

choices: 22: VTOL Standard (separate fixed rotors for hover and cruise flight)

MAV_USEHILGPS.summary: Use/Accept HIL GPS message even if not in HIL mode
MAV_USEHILGPS.description: If set to 1 incoming HIL GPS messages are parsed.

MBE_ENABLE.description:
This enables continuous calibration of the magnetometers
before takeoff using gyro data.

MBE_LEARN_GAIN.description:
Increase to make the estimator more responsive
Decrease to make the estimator more robust to noise

MAN_ARM_GESTURE.description:
This determines if moving the left stick to the lower right
arms and to the lower left disarms the vehicle.

MAN_DEADZONE.summary: Deadzone for sticks (only specific use cases)
MAN_DEADZONE.description:
Range around stick center ignored to prevent
vehicle drift from stick hardware inaccuracy.
Does not apply to any precise constant input like
throttle and attitude or rate piloting.

MAN_KILL_GEST_T.summary: Trigger time for kill stick gesture
MAN_KILL_GEST_T.description:
The timeout for holding the left stick to the lower left
and the right stick to the lower right at the same time until the gesture
kills the actuators one-way.
A negative value disables the feature.

MIS_COMMAND_TOUT.summary: Timeout to allow the payload to execute the mission command
MIS_COMMAND_TOUT.description:
Ensure:
gripper: NAV_CMD_DO_GRIPPER
has released before continuing mission.
winch: CMD_DO_WINCH
has delivered before continuing mission.
gimbal: CMD_DO_GIMBAL_MANAGER_PITCHYAW
has reached the commanded orientation before beginning to take pictures.

MIS_DIST_1WP.summary: Maximal horizontal distance from Home to first waypoint
MIS_DIST_1WP.description:
There will be a warning message if the current waypoint is more distant than MIS_DIST_1WP from Home.
Has no effect on mission validity.
Set a value of zero or less to disable.

MIS_LND_ABRT_ALT.description:
Minimum altitude above landing point that the vehicle will climb to after an aborted landing.
Then vehicle will loiter in this altitude until further command is received.
Only applies to fixed-wing vehicles.

MIS_MNT_YAW_CTL.summary: Enable yaw control of the mount. (Only affects multicopters and ROI mission items)
MIS_MNT_YAW_CTL.description:
If enabled, yaw commands will be sent to the mount and the vehicle will follow its heading towards the flight direction.
If disabled, the vehicle will yaw towards the ROI.

MIS_TAKEOFF_ALT.description:
This is the relative altitude the system will take off to
if not otherwise specified.

MIS_TKO_LAND_REQ.description:
Specifies if a mission has to contain a takeoff and/or mission landing.
Validity of configured takeoffs/landings is checked independently of the setting here.
choices: 3: Require a takeoff and a landing
4: Require both a takeoff and a landing, or neither
5: Same as previous when landed, in-air require landing only if no valid VTOL approach is present

MIS_YAW_ERR.summary: Max yaw error in degrees needed for waypoint heading acceptance

MIS_YAW_TMT.summary: Time in seconds we wait on reaching target heading at a waypoint if it is forced
MIS_YAW_TMT.description:
If set > 0 it will ignore the target heading for normal waypoint acceptance. If the
waypoint forces the heading the timeout will matter. For example on VTOL forwards transition.
Mainly useful for VTOLs that have less yaw authority and might not reach target
yaw in wind. Disabled by default.

NAV_ACC_RAD.description:
Default acceptance radius, overridden by acceptance radius of waypoint if set.
For fixed wing the npfg switch distance is used for horizontal acceptance.

NAV_FORCE_VT.summary: Force VTOL mode takeoff and land

NAV_FW_ALTL_RAD.summary: FW Altitude Acceptance Radius before a landing
NAV_FW_ALTL_RAD.description:
Altitude acceptance used for the last waypoint before a fixed-wing landing. This is usually smaller
than the standard vertical acceptance because close to the ground higher accuracy is required.

NAV_LOITER_RAD.description:
Default value of loiter radius in fixed-wing mode (e.g. for Loiter mode).
The direction of the loiter can be set via the sign: A positive value for
clockwise, negative for counter-clockwise.

NAV_MIN_GND_DIST.summary: Minimum height above ground during Mission and RTL
NAV_MIN_GND_DIST.description:
Minimum height above ground the vehicle is allowed to descend to during Mission and RTL,
excluding landing commands.
Requires a distance sensor to be set up.
Note: only prevents the vehicle from descending further, but does not force it to climb.
Set to a negative value to disable.

NAV_MIN_LTR_ALT.description:
This is the minimum altitude above Home the system will always obey in Loiter (Hold) mode if switched into this
mode without specifying an altitude (e.g. through Loiter switch on RC).
Doesn't affect Loiters that are part of Missions or that are entered through a reposition setpoint ("Go to").
Set to a negative value to disable.

NAV_TRAFF_AVOID.description:
Enabling this will allow the system to respond
to transponder data from e.g. ADSB transponders

NAV_TRAFF_A_HOR.summary: Set NAV TRAFFIC AVOID horizontal distance

NAV_TRAFF_A_VER.summary: Set NAV TRAFFIC AVOID vertical distance

NAV_TRAFF_COLL_T.description:
Minimum acceptable time until collsion.
Assumes constant speed over 3d distance.

MC_AIRMODE.description:
The air-mode enables the mixer to increase the total thrust of the multirotor
in order to keep attitude and rate control even at low and high throttle.
This function should be disabled during tuning as it will help the controller
to diverge if the closed-loop is unstable (i.e. the vehicle is not tuned yet).
Enabling air-mode for yaw requires the use of an arming switch.

MNT_DO_STAB.description:
Set to true for servo gimbal, false for passthrough.
This is required for a gimbal which is not capable of stabilizing itself
and relies on the IMU's attitude estimation.

MNT_MAN_PITCH.summary: Auxiliary channel to control pitch (in AUX input or manual mode)

MNT_MAN_ROLL.summary: Auxiliary channel to control roll (in AUX input or manual mode)

MNT_MAN_YAW.summary: Auxiliary channel to control yaw (in AUX input or manual mode)

MNT_MAV_COMPID.summary: Mavlink Component ID of the mount
MNT_MAV_COMPID.description: If MNT_MODE_OUT is MAVLink protocol v2, mount configure/control commands will be sent with this component ID.

MNT_MAV_SYSID.summary: Mavlink System ID of the mount
MNT_MAV_SYSID.description: If MNT_MODE_OUT is MAVLink gimbal protocol v1, mount configure/control commands will be sent with this target ID.

MNT_MAX_PITCH.summary: Max positive angle of pitch setpoint (only in MNT_MODE_OUT=AUX)
MNT_MAX_PITCH.description: Use output driver settings to calibrate (e.g. PWM_CENT/_MIN/_MAX).

MNT_MIN_PITCH.summary: Min negative angle of pitch setpoint (only in MNT_MODE_OUT=AUX)
MNT_MIN_PITCH.description: Use output driver settings to calibrate (e.g. PWM_CENT/_MIN/_MAX).

MNT_MODE_IN.description:
This is the protocol used between the ground station and the autopilot.
Recommended is Auto, RC only or MAVLink gimbal protocol v2.
The rest will be deprecated.
choices: 0: Auto (RC and MAVLink gimbal protocol v2)

MNT_MODE_OUT.description:
This is the protocol used between the autopilot and a connected gimbal.
Recommended is the MAVLink gimbal protocol v2 if the gimbal supports it.

MNT_RANGE_ROLL.summary: Range of roll channel output (only in MNT_MODE_OUT=AUX)
MNT_RANGE_ROLL.description: Use output driver settings to calibrate (e.g. PWM_CENT/_MIN/_MAX). Note that only symmetric angular ranges are supported.

MNT_RANGE_YAW.summary: Range of yaw channel output (only in MNT_MODE_OUT=AUX)
MNT_RANGE_YAW.description: Use output driver settings to calibrate (e.g. PWM_CENT/_MIN/_MAX). Note that only symmetric angular ranges are supported.

MNT_RATE_PITCH.summary: Angular pitch rate for manual input in degrees/second
MNT_RATE_PITCH.description: Full stick input [-1..1] translats to [-pitch rate..pitch rate].

MNT_RATE_YAW.summary: Angular yaw rate for manual input in degrees/second
MNT_RATE_YAW.description: Full stick input [-1..1] translats to [-yaw rate..yaw rate].

MNT_RC_IN_MODE.summary: Input mode for RC gimbal input

MNT_TAU.summary: Alpha filter time constant defining the convergence rate (in seconds) for open-loop AUX mount control
MNT_TAU.description:
Use when no angular position feedback is available.
With MNT_MODE_OUT set to AUX, the mount operates in open-loop and directly commands the servo output.
Parameters must be tuned for the specific servo to approximate its speed and response.

MC_ACRO_EXPO.summary: Acro mode roll, pitch expo factor
MC_ACRO_EXPO.description:
Exponential factor for tuning the input curve shape.
0 Purely linear input curve
1 Purely cubic input curve

MC_ACRO_EXPO_Y.description:
Exponential factor for tuning the input curve shape.
0 Purely linear input curve
1 Purely cubic input curve

MC_ACRO_P_MAX.description: Full stick deflection leads to this rate.

MC_ACRO_R_MAX.description: Full stick deflection leads to this rate.

MC_ACRO_SUPEXPO.summary: Acro mode roll, pitch super expo factor
MC_ACRO_SUPEXPO.description:
"Superexponential" factor for refining the input curve shape tuned using MC_ACRO_EXPO.
0 Pure Expo function
0.7 reasonable shape enhancement for intuitive stick feel
0.95 very strong bent input curve only near maxima have effect

MC_ACRO_SUPEXPOY.summary: Acro mode yaw super expo factor
MC_ACRO_SUPEXPOY.description:
"Superexponential" factor for refining the input curve shape tuned using MC_ACRO_EXPO_Y.
0 Pure Expo function
0.7 reasonable shape enhancement for intuitive stick feel
0.95 very strong bent input curve only near maxima have effect

MC_ACRO_Y_MAX.description: Full stick deflection leads to this rate.

MC_PITCHRATE_MAX.description:
Limit for pitch rate in manual and auto modes (except acro).
Has effect for large rotations in autonomous mode, to avoid large control
output and mixer saturation.
This is not only limited by the vehicle's properties, but also by the maximum
measurement rate of the gyro.

MC_PITCH_P.description: Pitch proportional gain, i.e. desired angular speed in rad/s for error 1 rad.

MC_ROLLRATE_MAX.description:
Limit for roll rate in manual and auto modes (except acro).
Has effect for large rotations in autonomous mode, to avoid large control
output and mixer saturation.
This is not only limited by the vehicle's properties, but also by the maximum
measurement rate of the gyro.

MC_ROLL_P.description: Roll proportional gain, i.e. desired angular speed in rad/s for error 1 rad.

MC_YAW_P.description: Yaw proportional gain, i.e. desired angular speed in rad/s for error 1 rad.

MC_YAW_WEIGHT.description:
A fraction [0,1] deprioritizing yaw compared to roll and pitch in non-linear attitude control.
Deprioritizing yaw is necessary because multicopters have much less control authority
in yaw compared to the other axes and it makes sense because yaw is not critical for
stable hovering or 3D navigation.
For yaw control tuning use MC_YAW_P. This ratio has no impact on the yaw gain.

MPC_YAWRAUTO_ACC.summary: Maximum yaw acceleration in autonomous modes
MPC_YAWRAUTO_ACC.description:
Limits the acceleration of the yaw setpoint to avoid large
control output and mixer saturation.

MPC_YAWRAUTO_MAX.summary: Maximum yaw rate in autonomous modes
MPC_YAWRAUTO_MAX.description:
Limits the rate of change of the yaw setpoint to avoid large
control output and mixer saturation.

CP_DELAY.summary: Average delay of the range sensor message plus the tracking delay of the position controller in seconds

CP_DIST.summary: Minimum distance the vehicle should keep to all obstacles
CP_DIST.description: Only used in Position mode. Collision avoidance is disabled by setting this parameter to a negative value

CP_GO_NO_DATA.summary: Boolean to allow moving into directions where there is no sensor data (outside FOV)

CP_GUIDE_ANG.summary: Angle left/right from the commanded setpoint by which the collision prevention algorithm can choose to change the setpoint direction

MC_MAN_TILT_TAU.summary: Manual tilt input filter time constant
MC_MAN_TILT_TAU.description: Setting this parameter to 0 disables the filter

MPC_ACC_DECOUPLE.description:
Set to decouple tilt from vertical acceleration.
This provides smoother flight but slightly worse tracking in position and auto modes.
Unset if accurate position tracking during dynamic maneuvers is more important than a smooth flight.

MPC_ACC_DOWN_MAX.summary: Maximum downwards acceleration in climb rate controlled modes

MPC_ACC_HOR.summary: Acceleration for autonomous and for manual modes
MPC_ACC_HOR.description: When piloting manually, this parameter is only used in MPC_POS_MODE Acceleration based.

MPC_ACC_HOR_MAX.description:
MPC_POS_MODE
1 just deceleration
4 not used, use MPC_ACC_HOR instead

MPC_ACC_UP_MAX.summary: Maximum upwards acceleration in climb rate controlled modes

MPC_ALT_MODE.description:
Control height
0: relative earth frame origin which may drift due to sensors
1: relative to ground (requires distance sensor) which changes with terrain variation.
It will revert to relative earth frame if the distance to ground estimate becomes invalid.
2: relative to ground (requires distance sensor) when stationary
and relative to earth frame when moving horizontally.
The speed threshold is MPC_HOLD_MAX_XY

MPC_HOLD_MAX_XY.summary: Maximum horizontal velocity for which position hold is enabled (use 0 to disable check)
MPC_HOLD_MAX_XY.description: Only used with MPC_POS_MODE Direct velocity or MPC_ALT_MODE 2

MPC_HOLD_MAX_Z.summary: Maximum vertical velocity for which position hold is enabled (use 0 to disable check)

MPC_JERK_AUTO.description:
Limit the maximum jerk of the vehicle (how fast the acceleration can change).
A lower value leads to smoother vehicle motions but also limited agility.

MPC_JERK_MAX.summary: Maximum horizontal and vertical jerk in Position/Altitude mode
MPC_JERK_MAX.description:
Limit the maximum jerk (acceleration change) of the vehicle.
A lower value leads to smoother motions but limits agility.
Setting this to the maximum value essentially disables the limit.
Only used with MPC_POS_MODE Acceleration based.

MPC_LAND_ALT1.summary: Altitude for 1. step of slow landing (descend)
MPC_LAND_ALT1.description:
Below this altitude descending velocity gets limited to a value
between "MPC_Z_VEL_MAX_DN" (or "MPC_Z_V_AUTO_DN") and "MPC_LAND_SPEED"
Value needs to be higher than "MPC_LAND_ALT2"

MPC_LAND_ALT2.summary: Altitude for 2. step of slow landing (landing)
MPC_LAND_ALT2.description:
Below this altitude descending velocity gets
limited to "MPC_LAND_SPEED"
Value needs to be lower than "MPC_LAND_ALT1"

MPC_LAND_ALT3.summary: Altitude for 3. step of slow landing
MPC_LAND_ALT3.description:
If a valid distance sensor measurement to the ground is available,
limit descending velocity to "MPC_LAND_CRWL" below this altitude.

MPC_LAND_CRWL.description: Used below MPC_LAND_ALT3 if distance sensor data is availabe.

MPC_LAND_RADIUS.description:
When nudging is enabled (see MPC_LAND_RC_HELP), this defines the maximum
allowed horizontal displacement from the original landing point.
- If inside of the radius, only allow nudging inputs that do not move the vehicle outside of it.
- If outside of the radius, only allow nudging inputs that move the vehicle back towards it.
Set it to -1 for infinite radius.

MPC_LAND_RC_HELP.summary: Enable nudging based on user input during autonomous land routine
MPC_LAND_RC_HELP.description:
Using stick input the vehicle can be moved horizontally and yawed.
The descend speed is amended:
stick full up - 0
stick centered - MPC_LAND_SPEED
stick full down - 2 * MPC_LAND_SPEED
Manual override during auto modes has to be disabled to use this feature (see COM_RC_OVERRIDE).

MPC_MANTHR_MIN.summary: Minimum collective thrust in Stabilized mode
MPC_MANTHR_MIN.description:
The value is mapped to the lowest throttle stick position in Stabilized mode.
Too low collective thrust leads to loss of roll/pitch/yaw torque control authority.
Airmode is used to keep torque authority with zero thrust (see MC_AIRMODE).

MPC_MAN_TILT_MAX.summary: Maximal tilt angle in Stabilized, Altitude and Altitude Cruise mode

MPC_MAN_Y_MAX.summary: Max manual yaw rate for Stabilized, Altitude, Position mode

MPC_MAN_Y_TAU.summary: Manual yaw rate input filter time constant
MPC_MAN_Y_TAU.description:
Not used in Stabilized mode
Setting this parameter to 0 disables the filter

MPC_POS_MODE.description:
The supported sub-modes are:
Direct velocity:
Sticks directly map to velocity setpoints without smoothing.
Also applies to vertical direction and Altitude mode.
Useful for velocity control tuning.
Acceleration based:
Sticks map to acceleration and there's a virtual brake drag

MPC_THR_CURVE.summary: Thrust curve mapping in Stabilized Mode
MPC_THR_CURVE.description:
Defines how the throttle stick is mapped to collective thrust in Stabilized mode.
Rescale to hover thrust estimate:
Stick input is linearly rescaled, such that a centered throttle stick corresponds to the hover thrust estimator's output.
No rescale:
Directly map the stick 1:1 to the output.
Can be useful with very low hover thrust which leads to much distortion and the upper half getting sensitive.
Rescale to hover thrust parameter:
Similar to rescaling to the hover thrust estimate, but it uses the hover thrust parameter value (see MPC_THR_HOVER) instead of estimated value.
With MPC_THR_HOVER 0.5 it's equivalent to No rescale.

MPC_THR_HOVER.description:
Mapped to center throttle stick in Stabilized mode (see MPC_THR_CURVE).
Used for initialization of the hover thrust estimator.
The estimated hover thrust is used as base for zero vertical acceleration in altitude control.
The hover thrust is important for land detection to work correctly.

MPC_THR_MAX.summary: Maximum collective thrust in climb rate controlled modes
MPC_THR_MAX.description: Limit allowed thrust e.g. for indoor test of overpowered vehicle.

MPC_THR_MIN.summary: Minimum collective thrust in climb rate controlled modes
MPC_THR_MIN.description:
Too low thrust leads to loss of roll/pitch/yaw torque control authority.
With airmode enabled this parameters can be set to 0
while still keeping torque authority (see MC_AIRMODE).

MPC_THR_XY_MARG.description:
Margin that is kept for horizontal control when higher priority vertical thrust is saturated.
To avoid completely starving horizontal control with high vertical error.

MPC_TILTMAX_AIR.description:
Absolute maximum for all velocity or acceleration controlled modes.
Any higher value is truncated.

MPC_TILTMAX_LND.summary: Maximum tilt during inital takeoff ramp
MPC_TILTMAX_LND.description: Tighter tilt limit during takeoff to avoid tip over.

MPC_TKO_RAMP_T.description:
Increasing this value will make climb rate controlled takeoff slower.
If it's too slow the drone might scratch the ground and tip over.
A time constant of 0 disables the ramp

MPC_VELD_LP.summary: Velocity derivative low pass cutoff frequency
MPC_VELD_LP.description: A value of 0 disables the filter.

MPC_VEL_LP.description: A value of 0 disables the filter.

MPC_VEL_MANUAL.summary: Maximum horizontal velocity setpoint in Position mode
MPC_VEL_MANUAL.description:
Must be smaller than MPC_XY_VEL_MAX.
The maximum sideways and backward speed can be set differently
using MPC_VEL_MAN_SIDE and MPC_VEL_MAN_BACK, respectively.

MPC_VEL_MAN_BACK.summary: Maximum backward velocity in Position mode
MPC_VEL_MAN_BACK.description:
If set to a negative value or larger than
MPC_VEL_MANUAL then MPC_VEL_MANUAL is used.

MPC_VEL_MAN_SIDE.summary: Maximum sideways velocity in Position mode
MPC_VEL_MAN_SIDE.description:
If set to a negative value or larger than
MPC_VEL_MANUAL then MPC_VEL_MANUAL is used.

MPC_VEL_NF_BW.description: A value of 0 disables the filter.

MPC_VEL_NF_FRQ.description:
The center frequency for the 2nd order notch filter on the velocity.
A value of 0 disables the filter.

MPC_XY_CRUISE.summary: Default horizontal velocity in autonomous modes
MPC_XY_CRUISE.description: e.g. in Missions, RTL, Goto if the waypoint does not specify differently

MPC_XY_ERR_MAX.summary: Maximum horizontal error allowed by the trajectory generator
MPC_XY_ERR_MAX.description:
The integration speed of the trajectory setpoint is linearly
reduced with the horizontal position tracking error. When the
error is above this parameter, the integration of the
trajectory is stopped to wait for the drone.
This value can be adjusted depending on the tracking
capabilities of the vehicle.

MPC_XY_P.summary: Proportional gain for horizontal position error
MPC_XY_P.description: Defined as corrective velocity in m/s per m position error

MPC_XY_TRAJ_P.summary: Proportional gain for horizontal trajectory position error

MPC_XY_VEL_ALL.description:
If set to a value greater than zero, other parameters are automatically set (such as
MPC_XY_VEL_MAX or MPC_VEL_MANUAL).
If set to a negative value, the existing individual parameters are used.

MPC_XY_VEL_D_ACC.summary: Differential gain for horizontal velocity error
MPC_XY_VEL_D_ACC.description: Defined as corrective acceleration in m/s^2 per m/s^2 velocity derivative

MPC_XY_VEL_I_ACC.summary: Integral gain for horizontal velocity error
MPC_XY_VEL_I_ACC.description:
Defined as correction acceleration in m/s^2 per m velocity integral
Allows to eliminate steady state errors in disturbances like wind.

MPC_XY_VEL_MAX.description:
Absolute maximum for all velocity controlled modes.
Any higher value is truncated.

MPC_XY_VEL_P_ACC.summary: Proportional gain for horizontal velocity error
MPC_XY_VEL_P_ACC.description: Defined as corrective acceleration in m/s^2 per m/s velocity error

MPC_Z_P.summary: Proportional gain for vertical position error
MPC_Z_P.description: Defined as corrective velocity in m/s per m position error

MPC_Z_VEL_ALL.description:
If set to a value greater than zero, other parameters are automatically set (such as
MPC_Z_VEL_MAX_UP or MPC_LAND_SPEED).
If set to a negative value, the existing individual parameters are used.

MPC_Z_VEL_D_ACC.summary: Differential gain for vertical velocity error
MPC_Z_VEL_D_ACC.description: Defined as corrective acceleration in m/s^2 per m/s^2 velocity derivative

MPC_Z_VEL_I_ACC.summary: Integral gain for vertical velocity error
MPC_Z_VEL_I_ACC.description: Defined as corrective acceleration in m/s^2 per m velocity integral

MPC_Z_VEL_MAX_DN.description:
Absolute maximum for all climb rate controlled modes.
In manually piloted modes full stick deflection commands this velocity.
For default autonomous velocity see MPC_Z_V_AUTO_UP

MPC_Z_VEL_MAX_UP.description:
Absolute maximum for all climb rate controlled modes.
In manually piloted modes full stick deflection commands this velocity.
For default autonomous velocity see MPC_Z_V_AUTO_UP

MPC_Z_VEL_P_ACC.summary: Proportional gain for vertical velocity error
MPC_Z_VEL_P_ACC.description: Defined as corrective acceleration in m/s^2 per m/s velocity error

SYS_VEHICLE_RESP.description:
Changes the overall responsiveness of the vehicle.
The higher the value, the faster the vehicle will react.
If set to a value greater than zero, other parameters are automatically set (such as
the acceleration or jerk limits).
If set to a negative value, the existing individual parameters are used.

WV_ROLL_MIN.summary: Minimum roll angle setpoint for weathervane controller to demand a yaw-rate

WV_YRATE_MAX.summary: Maximum yawrate the weathervane controller is allowed to demand

MC_SLOW_DEF_HVEL.description:

no aux channel is mapped and
no limit is commanded through MAVLink.

MC_SLOW_DEF_VVEL.description:

MC_SLOW_DEF_YAWR.description:

MC_SLOW_MAP_YAWR.summary: Manual input mapped to scale yaw rate in position slow mode

MC_SLOW_MIN_VVEL.description: The lowest input maps and is clamped to this velocity.

MC_BAT_SCALE_EN.description:
This compensates for voltage drop of the battery over time by attempting to
normalize performance across the operating range of the battery. The copter
should constantly behave as if it was fully charged with reduced max acceleration
at lower battery percentages. i.e. if hover is at 0.5 throttle at 100% battery,
it will still be 0.5 at 60% battery.

MC_PITCHRATE_D.description: Pitch rate differential gain. Small values help reduce fast oscillations. If value is too big oscillations will appear again.

MC_PITCHRATE_I.description: Pitch rate integral gain. Can be set to compensate static thrust difference or gravity center offset.

MC_PITCHRATE_K.description:
Global gain of the controller.
This gain scales the P, I and D terms of the controller:
output = MC_PITCHRATE_K * (MC_PITCHRATE_P * error
+ MC_PITCHRATE_I * error_integral
+ MC_PITCHRATE_D * error_derivative)
Set MC_PITCHRATE_P=1 to implement a PID in the ideal form.
Set MC_PITCHRATE_K=1 to implement a PID in the parallel form.

MC_PITCHRATE_P.description: Pitch rate proportional gain, i.e. control output for angular speed error 1 rad/s.

MC_PR_INT_LIM.description: Pitch rate integrator limit. Can be set to increase the amount of integrator available to counteract disturbances or reduced to improve settling time after large pitch moment trim changes.

MC_ROLLRATE_D.description: Roll rate differential gain. Small values help reduce fast oscillations. If value is too big oscillations will appear again.

MC_ROLLRATE_I.description: Roll rate integral gain. Can be set to compensate static thrust difference or gravity center offset.

MC_ROLLRATE_K.description:
Global gain of the controller.
This gain scales the P, I and D terms of the controller:
output = MC_ROLLRATE_K * (MC_ROLLRATE_P * error
+ MC_ROLLRATE_I * error_integral
+ MC_ROLLRATE_D * error_derivative)
Set MC_ROLLRATE_P=1 to implement a PID in the ideal form.
Set MC_ROLLRATE_K=1 to implement a PID in the parallel form.

MC_ROLLRATE_P.description: Roll rate proportional gain, i.e. control output for angular speed error 1 rad/s.

MC_RR_INT_LIM.description: Roll rate integrator limit. Can be set to increase the amount of integrator available to counteract disturbances or reduced to improve settling time after large roll moment trim changes.

MC_YAWRATE_D.description: Yaw rate differential gain. Small values help reduce fast oscillations. If value is too big oscillations will appear again.

MC_YAWRATE_I.description: Yaw rate integral gain. Can be set to compensate static thrust difference or gravity center offset.

MC_YAWRATE_K.description:

Set MC_YAWRATE_P=1 to implement a PID in the ideal form.
Set MC_YAWRATE_K=1 to implement a PID in the parallel form.

MC_YAWRATE_P.description: Yaw rate proportional gain, i.e. control output for angular speed error 1 rad/s.

MC_YAW_TQ_CUTOFF.summary: Low pass filter cutoff frequency for yaw torque setpoint
MC_YAW_TQ_CUTOFF.description:
Reduces vibrations by lowering high frequency torque caused by rotor acceleration.
0 disables the filter

MC_YR_INT_LIM.description: Yaw rate integrator limit. Can be set to increase the amount of integrator available to counteract disturbances or reduced to improve settling time after large yaw moment trim changes.

OSD_CH_HEIGHT.description:
Controls the vertical position of the crosshair display.
Resolution is limited by OSD to 15 discrete values. Negative
values will display the crosshairs below the horizon

OSD_DWELL_TIME.description: Amount of time in milliseconds to dwell at the beginning of the display, when scrolling.

OSD_LOG_LEVEL.description: Minimum security of log level to display on the OSD.

OSD_RC_STICK.description: Forward RC stick input to VTX when disarmed

OSD_SCROLL_RATE.description:
Scroll rate in milliseconds for OSD messages longer than available character width.
This is lower-bounded by the nominal loop rate of this module.

THR_MDL_FAC.summary: Thrust to motor control signal model parameter
THR_MDL_FAC.description:
Parameter used to model the nonlinear relationship between
motor control signal (e.g. PWM) and static thrust.
The model is: rel_thrust = factor * rel_signal^2 + (1-factor) * rel_signal,
where rel_thrust is the normalized thrust between 0 and 1, and
rel_signal is the relative motor control signal between 0 and 1.

PD_GRIPPER_TO.summary: Timeout for successful gripper actuation acknowledgement
PD_GRIPPER_TO.description:
Maximum time Gripper will wait while the successful griper actuation isn't recognised.
If the gripper has no feedback sensor, it will simply wait for
this time before considering gripper actuation successful and publish a
'VehicleCommandAck' signaling successful gripper action

PLD_BTOUT.description: Time after which the landing target is considered lost without any new measurements.

PLD_FAPPR_ALT.description: Allow final approach (without horizontal positioning) if losing landing target closer than this to the ground.

PLD_HACC_RAD.description: Start descending if closer above landing target than this.

PLD_MAX_SRCH.description: Maximum number of times to search for the landing target if it is lost during the precision landing.

PLD_SRCH_ALT.description: Altitude above home to which to climb when searching for the landing target.

PLD_SRCH_TOUT.description: Time allowed to search for the landing target before falling back to normal landing.

PP_LOOKAHD_GAIN.summary: Tuning parameter for the pure pursuit controller
PP_LOOKAHD_GAIN.description: Lower value -> More aggressive controller (beware overshoot/oscillations)

PP_LOOKAHD_MAX.summary: Maximum lookahead distance for the pure pursuit controller

PP_LOOKAHD_MIN.summary: Minimum lookahead distance for the pure pursuit controller

RC_CHAN_CNT.description:
This parameter is used by Ground Station software to save the number
of channels which were used during RC calibration. It is only meant
for ground station use.

RC_FAILS_THR.description:
Use RC_MAP_FAILSAFE to specify which channel is used to indicate RC loss via this threshold.
By default this is the throttle channel.
Set to a PWM value slightly above the PWM value for the channel (e.g. throttle) in a failsafe event,
but below the minimum PWM value for the channel during normal operation.
Note: The default value of 0 disables the feature (it is below the expected range).

RC_MAP_ENG_MOT.summary: RC channel to engage the main motor (for helicopters)

RC_MAP_FAILSAFE.description:
Configures which RC channel is used by the receiver to indicate the signal was lost
(on receivers that use output a fixed signal value to report lost signal).
If set to 0, the channel mapped to throttle is used.
Use RC_FAILS_THR to set the threshold indicating lost signal. By default it's below
the expected range and hence disabled.

RC_MAP_PARAM1.description:
Can be used for parameter tuning with the RC. This one is further referenced as the 1st parameter channel.
Set to 0 to deactivate *

RC_MAP_PARAM2.description:
Can be used for parameter tuning with the RC. This one is further referenced as the 2nd parameter channel.

RC_MAP_PARAM3.description:

RC_MAP_PITCH.description:

RC_MAP_ROLL.description:

RC_MAP_THROTTLE.description:

RC_MAP_YAW.description:

RC_RSSI_PWM_CHAN.summary: PWM input channel that provides RSSI

RC_MAP_ARM_SW.description:
Use it to arm/disarm via switch instead of default throttle stick. If this is
assigned, arming and disarming via stick is disabled.

RC_MAP_FLTMODE.description:
If this parameter is non-zero, flight modes are only selected
by this channel and are assigned to six slots.

RC_MAP_FLTM_BTN.description:
This bitmask allows to specify multiple channels for changing flight modes using
momentary buttons. Each channel is assigned to a mode slot ((lowest channel = slot 1).
The resulting modes for each slot X is defined by the COM_FLTMODEX parameters.
The functionality can be used only if RC_MAP_FLTMODE is disabled.
The maximum number of available slots and hence bits set in the mask is 6.

RC_MAP_KILL_SW.description:
This channel immediately sets all outputs to their disarmed values, parachutes are NOT deployed.
Unlike termination this can be undone. Quickly flipping the switch back restores control.
System auto-disarms after COM_KILL_DISARM seconds, preflight checks and re-arming are then required.

RC_MAP_MODE_SW.description:
This is the main flight mode selector.
The channel index (starting from 1 for channel 1) indicates
which channel should be used for deciding about the main mode.
A value of zero indicates the switch is not assigned.

RC_MAP_TERM_SW.description:
This channel triggers irreversible flight termination:
All outputs are disabled and set to their failsafe values (disarmed by default)
and MAVLink parachutes are triggered.
Unlike a kill switch, this cannot be undone until system reboot. Use with caution.

RTL_CONE_ANG.summary: Half-angle of the return mode altitude cone
RTL_CONE_ANG.description:
Defines the half-angle of a cone centered around the destination position that
affects the altitude at which the vehicle returns.
choices: 0: No cone, always climb to RTL_RETURN_ALT above destination.
90: Only climb to at least RTL_DESCEND_ALT above destination.

RTL_DESCEND_ALT.description:
Descend to this altitude (above destination position) after return, and wait for time defined in RTL_LAND_DELAY.
Land (i.e. slowly descend) from this altitude if autolanding allowed.
VTOLs do transition to hover in this altitdue above the landing point.

RTL_LAND_DELAY.description:
Delay before landing (after initial descent) in Return mode.
If set to -1 the system will not land but loiter at RTL_DESCEND_ALT.

RTL_LOITER_RAD.description: Set the radius for loitering to a safe altitude for VTOL transition.

RTL_MIN_DIST.summary: Horizontal radius from return point within which special rules for return mode apply
RTL_MIN_DIST.description:
The return altitude will be calculated based on RTL_CONE_ANG parameter.
The yaw setpoint will switch to the one defined by corresponding waypoint.

RTL_PLD_MD.description:
Use precision landing when doing an RTL landing phase.
This setting does not apply for RTL destinations planned as part of a mission.

RTL_RETURN_ALT.description:
Default minimum altitude above destination (e.g. home, safe point, landing pattern) for return flight.
The vehicle will climb to this altitude when Return mode is enganged, unless it currently is flying higher already.
This is affected by RTL_MIN_DIST and RTL_CONE_ANG.

RTL_TYPE.description: Return mode destination and flight path (home location, rally point, mission landing pattern, reverse mission)
choices: 0: Return to closest safe point (home or rally point) via direct path.

1: Return to closest safe point other than home (mission landing pattern or rally point), via direct path. If no mission landing or rally points are defined return home via direct path. Always choose closest safe landing point if vehicle is a VTOL in hover mode.
2: Return to a planned mission landing, if available, using the mission path, else return to home via the reverse mission path. Do not consider rally points.
3: Return via direct path to closest destination: home, start of mission landing pattern or safe point. If the destination is a mission landing pattern, follow the pattern to land.
4: Return to the planned mission landing, or to home via the reverse mission path, whichever is closer by counting waypoints. Do not consider rally points.
5: Return directly to safe landing point (do not consider mission landing and Home)

RTL_APPR_FORCE.description: Only consider RTL point, if it has an approach defined.

RTL_TIME_FACTOR.summary: RTL time estimate safety margin factor
RTL_TIME_FACTOR.description:
Safety factor that is used to scale the actual RTL time estimate.
Time with margin = RTL_TIME_FACTOR * time + RTL_TIME_MARGIN

RTL_TIME_MARGIN.summary: RTL time estimate safety margin offset
RTL_TIME_MARGIN.description:
Margin that is added to the time estimate, after it has already been scaled
Time with margin = RTL_TIME_FACTOR * time + RTL_TIME_MARGIN

RA_ACC_RAD_GAIN.description:
The geometric ideal acceptance radius is multiplied by this factor
to account for kinematic and dynamic effects.
Higher value -> The rover starts to cut the corner earlier.

RA_ACC_RAD_MAX.summary: Maximum acceptance radius for the waypoints
RA_ACC_RAD_MAX.description:
The controller scales the acceptance radius based on the angle between
the previous, current and next waypoint.
Higher value -> smoother trajectory at the cost of how close the rover gets
to the waypoint (Set to -1 to disable corner cutting).

RA_WHEEL_BASE.description: Distance from the front to the rear axle.

RO_YAW_P.summary: Proportional gain for closed loop yaw controller

RD_TRANS_DRV_TRN.summary: Yaw error threshhold to switch from driving to spot turning
RD_TRANS_DRV_TRN.description:
This threshold is used for the state machine to switch from driving to turning based on the
error between the desired and actual yaw. It is also used as the threshold whether the rover should come
to a smooth stop at the next waypoint. This slow down effect is active if the angle between the
line segments from prevWP-currWP and currWP-nextWP is smaller then 180 - RD_TRANS_DRV_TRN.

RD_TRANS_TRN_DRV.summary: Yaw error threshhold to switch from spot turning to driving
RD_TRANS_TRN_DRV.description:
This threshold is used for the state machine to switch from turning to driving based on the
error between the desired and actual yaw.

RD_WHEEL_TRACK.description: Distance from the center of the right wheel to the center of the left wheel.

RD_YAW_STK_GAIN.summary: Yaw stick gain for Manual mode
RD_YAW_STK_GAIN.description: Assign value <1.0 to decrease stick response for yaw control.

RM_COURSE_CTL_TH.summary: Threshold to update course control in manual position mode
RM_COURSE_CTL_TH.description:
Threshold for the angle between the active cruise direction and the cruise direction given
by the stick inputs.
This can be understood as a deadzone for the combined stick inputs for forward/backwards
and lateral speed which defines a course direction.

RM_WHEEL_TRACK.description: Distance from the center of the right wheel to the center of the left wheel.

RM_YAW_STK_GAIN.summary: Yaw stick gain for Manual mode
RM_YAW_STK_GAIN.description: Assign value <1.0 to decrease stick response for yaw control.

RO_YAW_ACCEL_LIM.description:
Used to cap how quickly the magnitude of yaw rate setpoints can increase.
Set to -1 to disable.

RO_YAW_DECEL_LIM.description:
Used to cap how quickly the magnitude of yaw rate setpoints can decrease.
Set to -1 to disable.

RO_YAW_EXPO.description:
Exponential factor for tuning the input curve shape.
0 Purely linear input curve
1 Purely cubic input curve

RO_YAW_RATE_CORR.description:
Multiplicative correction factor for the feedforward mapping of the yaw rate controller.
Increase this value (x > 1) if the measured yaw rate is lower than the setpoint, decrease (0 < x < 1) otherwise.
Note: Tuning this is particularly useful for skid-steered rovers, or rovers with misaligned wheels/steering axes
that cause a lot of friction when turning.

RO_YAW_RATE_I.summary: Integral gain for closed loop yaw rate controller

RO_YAW_RATE_LIM.description:
Used to cap yaw rate setpoints and map controller inputs to yaw rate setpoints
in Acro, Stabilized and Position mode.

RO_YAW_RATE_P.summary: Proportional gain for closed loop yaw rate controller

RO_YAW_RATE_TH.description: The minimum threshold for the yaw rate measurement not to be interpreted as zero.

RO_YAW_STICK_DZ.description: Percentage of stick input range that will be interpreted as zero around the stick centered value.

RO_YAW_SUPEXPO.description:
"Superexponential" factor for refining the input curve shape tuned using RO_YAW_EXPO.
0 Pure Expo function
0.7 reasonable shape enhancement for intuitive stick feel
0.95 very strong bent input curve only near maxima have effect

RO_ACCEL_LIM.description:
Set to -1 to disable.
For mecanum rovers this limit is used for longitudinal and lateral acceleration.

RO_DECEL_LIM.description:
Set to -1 to disable.
Note that if it is disabled the rover will not slow down when approaching waypoints in auto modes.
For mecanum rovers this limit is used for longitudinal and lateral deceleration.

RO_JERK_LIM.description:
Set to -1 to disable.
Note that if it is disabled the rover will not slow down when approaching waypoints in auto modes.
For mecanum rovers this limit is used for longitudinal and lateral jerk.

RO_MAX_THR_SPEED.summary: Speed the rover drives at maximum throttle
RO_MAX_THR_SPEED.description: Used to linearly map speeds [m/s] to throttle values [-1. 1].

RO_SPEED_I.summary: Integral gain for ground speed controller

RO_SPEED_LIM.description: Used to cap speed setpoints and map controller inputs to speed setpoints in Position mode.

RO_SPEED_P.summary: Proportional gain for ground speed controller

RO_SPEED_RED.summary: Tuning parameter for the speed reduction based on the course error
RO_SPEED_RED.description:
Reduced_speed = RO_MAX_THR_SPEED * (1 - normalized_course_error * RO_SPEED_RED)
The normalized course error is the angle between the current course and the bearing setpoint
interpolated from [0, 180] -> [0, 1].
Higher value -> More speed reduction.
Note: This is also used to calculate the speed at which the vehicle arrives at a waypoint in auto modes.
Set to -1 to disable bearing error based speed reduction.

RO_SPEED_TH.description:
Set to -1 to disable.
The minimum threshold for the speed measurement not to be interpreted as zero.

RWTO_NUDGE.summary: Enable use of yaw stick for nudging the wheel during runway ground roll
RWTO_NUDGE.description:
This is useful when map, GNSS, or yaw errors on ground are misaligned with what the operator intends for takeoff course.
Particularly useful for skinny runways or if the wheel servo is a bit off trim.

RWTO_PSP.summary: Pitch setpoint during taxi / before takeoff rotation airspeed is reached
RWTO_PSP.description:
A taildragger with steerable wheel might need to pitch up
a little to keep its wheel on the ground before airspeed
to takeoff is reached.

RWTO_RAMP_TIME.summary: Throttle ramp up time for runway takeoff

RWTO_ROT_AIRSPD.description:
The calibrated airspeed threshold during the takeoff ground roll when the plane should start rotating (pitching up).
Must be less than the takeoff airspeed, will otherwise be capped at the takeoff airpeed (see FW_TKO_AIRSPD).
If set <= 0.0, defaults to 0.9 * takeoff airspeed (see FW_TKO_AIRSPD)

RWTO_ROT_TIME.description: This is the time desired to linearly ramp in takeoff pitch constraints during the takeoff rotation

SDLOG_BACKEND.description: If no logging is set the logger will not be started. Set bits true to enable: 0: SD card logging 1: Mavlink logging
choices: Bitmask: 0: SD card logging, 1: Mavlink logging

SDLOG_BOOT_BAT.description: When enabled, logging will not start from boot if battery power is not detected (e.g. powered via USB on a test bench). This prevents extraneous flight logs from being created during bench testing. Note that this only applies to log-from-boot modes. This has no effect on arm-based modes.

SDLOG_DIRS_MAX.summary: Maximum number of log directories to keep
SDLOG_DIRS_MAX.description: If there are more log directories than this value, the system will delete the oldest directories during startup. In addition, the system will delete old logs if there is not enough free space left. The minimum amount is 300 MB. If this is set to 0, old directories will only be removed if the free space falls below the minimum. Note: this does not apply to mission log files.

SDLOG_MISSION.description: If enabled, a small additional "mission" log file will be written to the SD card. The log contains just those messages that are useful for tasks like generating flight statistics and geotagging. The different modes can be used to further reduce the logged data (and thus the log file size). For example, choose geotagging mode to only log data required for geotagging. Note that the normal/full log is still created, and contains all the data in the mission log (and more).

SDLOG_MODE.description: Determines when to start and stop logging. By default, logging is started when arming the system, and stopped when disarming. Note: The logging start/end points that can be configured here only apply to SD logging. The mavlink backend is started/stopped independently of these points.

SDLOG_PROFILE.description: This integer bitmask controls the set and rates of logged topics. The default allows for general log analysis while keeping the log file size reasonably small. Enabling multiple sets leads to higher bandwidth requirements and larger log files. Set bits true to enable: 0 : Default set (used for general log analysis) 1 : Full rate estimator (EKF2) replay topics 2 : Topics for thermal calibration (high rate raw IMU and Baro sensor data) 3 : Topics for system identification (high rate actuator control and IMU data) 4 : Full rates for analysis of fast maneuvers (RC, attitude, rates and actuators) 5 : Debugging topics (debug_*.msg topics, for custom code) 6 : Topics for sensor comparison (low rate raw IMU, Baro and magnetometer data) 7 : Topics for computer vision and collision prevention 8 : Raw FIFO high-rate IMU (Gyro) 9 : Raw FIFO high-rate IMU (Accel) 10: Logging of mavlink tunnel message (useful for payload communication debugging)
choices: Bitmask: 0: Default set (general log analysis), 1: Estimator replay (EKF2), 2: Thermal calibration, 3: System identification, 4: High rate, 5: Debug, 6: Sensor comparison, 7: Computer Vision and Avoidance, 8: Raw FIFO high-rate IMU (Gyro), 9: Raw FIFO high-rate IMU (Accel), 10: Mavlink tunnel message logging, 11: High rate sensors

Pick the appropriate scaling from the datasheet.
this number defines the (linear) conversion from voltage
to Pascal (pa). For the MPXV7002DP this is 1000.
NOTE: If the sensor always registers zero, try switching
the static and dynamic tubes.

SENS_DPRES_REV.description:
Reverse the raw measurements of all differential pressure sensors.
This can be enabled if the sensors have static and dynamic ports swapped.

SENS_FLOW_MAXHGT.summary: Maximum height above ground when reliant on optical flow
SENS_FLOW_MAXHGT.description:
This parameter defines the maximum distance from ground at which the optical flow sensor operates reliably.
The height setpoint will be limited to be no greater than this value when the navigation system
is completely reliant on optical flow data and the height above ground estimate is valid.
The sensor may be usable above this height, but accuracy will progressively degrade.

SENS_FLOW_MAXR.summary: Magnitude of maximum angular flow rate reliably measurable by the optical flow sensor
SENS_FLOW_MAXR.description:
Optical flow data will not fused by the estimators if the magnitude of the flow rate exceeds this value and
control loops will be instructed to limit ground speed such that the flow rate produced by movement over ground
is less than 50% of this value.

SENS_FLOW_MINHGT.summary: Minimum height above ground when reliant on optical flow
SENS_FLOW_MINHGT.description:
This parameter defines the minimum distance from ground at which the optical flow sensor operates reliably.
The sensor may be usable below this height, but accuracy will progressively reduce to loss of focus.

IMU_ACCEL_CUTOFF.summary: Low pass filter cutoff frequency for accel
IMU_ACCEL_CUTOFF.description:
The cutoff frequency for the 2nd order butterworth filter on the primary accelerometer.
This only affects the signal sent to the controllers, not the estimators. 0 disables the filter.

IMU_DGYRO_CUTOFF.summary: Cutoff frequency for angular acceleration (D-Term filter)
IMU_DGYRO_CUTOFF.description:
The cutoff frequency for the 2nd order butterworth filter used on
the time derivative of the measured angular velocity, also known as
the D-term filter in the rate controller. The D-term uses the derivative of
the rate and thus is the most susceptible to noise. Therefore, using
a D-term filter allows to increase IMU_GYRO_CUTOFF, which
leads to reduced control latency and permits to increase the P gains.
A value of 0 disables the filter.

IMU_GYRO_CUTOFF.summary: Low pass filter cutoff frequency for gyro
IMU_GYRO_CUTOFF.description:
The cutoff frequency for the 2nd order butterworth filter on the primary gyro.
This only affects the angular velocity sent to the controllers, not the estimators.
It applies also to the angular acceleration (D-Term filter), see IMU_DGYRO_CUTOFF.
A value of 0 disables the filter.

IMU_GYRO_DNF_BW.summary: IMU gyro ESC notch filter bandwidth
IMU_GYRO_DNF_BW.description: Bandwidth per notch filter when using dynamic notch filtering with ESC RPM.

IMU_GYRO_DNF_EN.description:
Enable bank of dynamically updating notch filters.
Requires ESC RPM feedback or onboard FFT (IMU_GYRO_FFT_EN).

IMU_GYRO_DNF_HMC.summary: IMU gyro dynamic notch filter harmonics
IMU_GYRO_DNF_HMC.description: ESC RPM number of harmonics (multiples of RPM) for ESC RPM dynamic notch filtering.

IMU_GYRO_DNF_MIN.summary: IMU gyro dynamic notch filter minimum frequency
IMU_GYRO_DNF_MIN.description: Minimum notch filter frequency in Hz.

IMU_GYRO_NF0_BW.description:
The frequency width of the stop band for the 2nd order notch filter on the primary gyro.
See "IMU_GYRO_NF0_FRQ" to activate the filter and to set the notch frequency.
Applies to both angular velocity and angular acceleration sent to the controllers.

IMU_GYRO_NF0_FRQ.description:
The center frequency for the 2nd order notch filter on the primary gyro.
This filter can be enabled to avoid feedback amplification of structural resonances at a specific frequency.
This only affects the signal sent to the controllers, not the estimators.
Applies to both angular velocity and angular acceleration sent to the controllers.
See "IMU_GYRO_NF0_BW" to set the bandwidth of the filter.
A value of 0 disables the filter.

IMU_GYRO_NF1_BW.description:
The frequency width of the stop band for the 2nd order notch filter on the primary gyro.
See "IMU_GYRO_NF1_FRQ" to activate the filter and to set the notch frequency.
Applies to both angular velocity and angular acceleration sent to the controllers.

IMU_GYRO_NF1_FRQ.description:
The center frequency for the 2nd order notch filter on the primary gyro.
This filter can be enabled to avoid feedback amplification of structural resonances at a specific frequency.
This only affects the signal sent to the controllers, not the estimators.
Applies to both angular velocity and angular acceleration sent to the controllers.
See "IMU_GYRO_NF1_BW" to set the bandwidth of the filter.
A value of 0 disables the filter.

IMU_GYRO_RATEMAX.summary: Gyro control data maximum publication rate (inner loop rate)
IMU_GYRO_RATEMAX.description:
The maximum rate the gyro control data (vehicle_angular_velocity) will be
allowed to publish at. This is the loop rate for the rate controller and outputs.
Note: sensor data is always read and filtered at the full raw rate (eg commonly 8 kHz) regardless of this setting.

IMU_INTEG_RATE.description:
The rate at which raw IMU data is integrated to produce delta angles and delta velocities.
Recommended to set this to a multiple of the estimator update period (currently 10 ms for ekf2).

SENS_BARO_RATE.description:
Barometric air data maximum publication rate. This is an upper bound,
actual barometric data rate is still dependent on the sensor.

SENS_BAR_AUTOCAL.description: Automatically calibrate barometer based on the GNSS height

SENS_BOARD_ROT.description: This parameter defines the rotation of the FMU board relative to the platform.

SENS_BOARD_X_OFF.description:
Rotation from flight controller board to vehicle body frame.
This parameter gets set during the "level horizon" calibration or can be
set manually.

SENS_BOARD_Y_OFF.description:
Rotation from flight controller board to vehicle body frame.
This parameter gets set during the "level horizon" calibration or can be
set manually.

SENS_BOARD_Z_OFF.description:
Rotation from flight controller board to vehicle body frame.
Has to be set manually (not set by any calibration).

SENS_EXT_I2C_PRB.description: Probe for optional external I2C devices.

SENS_FLOW_RATE.description:
Optical flow data maximum publication rate. This is an upper bound,
actual optical flow data rate is still dependent on the sensor.

SENS_FLOW_ROT.description:
This parameter defines the yaw rotation of the optical flow relative to the vehicle body frame.
Zero rotation is defined as X on flow board pointing towards front of vehicle.

SENS_GPS_MASK.description:
Set bits in the following positions to set which GPS accuracy metrics will be used to calculate the blending weight. Set to zero to disable and always used first GPS instance.
0 : Set to true to use speed accuracy
1 : Set to true to use horizontal position accuracy
2 : Set to true to use vertical position accuracy
choices: Bitmask: 0: use speed accuracy, 1: use hpos accuracy, 2: use vpos accuracy

SENS_GPS_PRIME.description:
When no blending is active, this defines the preferred GPS receiver instance.
The GPS selection logic waits until the primary receiver is available to
send data to the EKF even if a secondary instance is already available.
The secondary instance is then only used if the primary one times out.
Accepted values:
-1 : Auto (equal priority for all instances)
0 : Main serial GPS instance
1 : Secondary serial GPS instance
2-127 : UAVCAN module node ID
This parameter has no effect if blending is active.

SENS_GPS_TAU.description: Sets the longest time constant that will be applied to the calculation of GPS position and height offsets used to correct data from multiple GPS data for steady state position differences.

SENS_IMU_AUTOCAL.description: Automatically initialize IMU (accel/gyro) calibration from bias estimates if available.

SENS_IMU_CLPNOTI.description: Notify the user if the IMU is clipping

SENS_INT_BARO_EN.description: For systems with an external barometer, this should be set to false to make sure that the external is used.

SENS_MAG_AUTOCAL.description: Automatically initialize magnetometer calibration from bias estimate if available.

SENS_MAG_AUTOROT.description: During calibration attempt to automatically determine the rotation of external magnetometers.

SENS_MAG_RATE.description:
Magnetometer data maximum publication rate. This is an upper bound,
actual magnetometer data rate is still dependent on the sensor.

SENS_MAG_SIDES.summary: Bitfield selecting mag sides for calibration
SENS_MAG_SIDES.description:
If set to two side calibration, only the offsets are estimated, the scale
calibration is left unchanged. Thus an initial six side calibration is
recommended.
Bits:
ORIENTATION_TAIL_DOWN = 1
ORIENTATION_NOSE_DOWN = 2
ORIENTATION_LEFT = 4
ORIENTATION_RIGHT = 8
ORIENTATION_UPSIDE_DOWN = 16
ORIENTATION_RIGHTSIDE_UP = 32

SIM_ARSPD_FAIL.summary: Dynamically simulate failure of airspeed sensor instance

SEP_AUTO_CONFIG.description:
By default, the receiver is automatically configured. Sometimes it may be used for multiple purposes.
If the offered parameters aren't sufficient, this parameter can be disabled to have full control of the receiver configuration.
A good way to use this is to enable automatic configuration, let the receiver be configured, and then disable it to make manual adjustments.

SEP_CONST_USAGE.description:
Choice of which constellations the receiver should use for PVT computation.
When this is 0, the constellation usage isn't changed.
choices: Bitmask: 0: GPS, 1: GLONASS, 2: Galileo, 3: SBAS, 4: BeiDou

SEP_DUMP_COMM.description:
Log raw communication between the driver and connected receivers.
For example, "To receiver" will log all commands and corrections sent by the driver to the receiver.

SEP_HARDW_SETUP.summary: Setup and expected use of the hardware
SEP_HARDW_SETUP.description:
Setup and expected use of the hardware.
- Default: Use two receivers as completely separate instances.
- Moving base: Use two receivers in a rover & moving base setup for heading.

SEP_LOG_FORCE.summary: Whether to overwrite or add to existing logging
SEP_LOG_FORCE.description: When the receiver is already set up to log data, this decides whether extra logged data should be added or overwrite existing data.

SEP_LOG_HZ.description: Select the frequency at which the connected receiver should log data to its internal storage.

SEP_LOG_LEVEL.description: Select the level of detail that needs to be logged by the receiver.

SEP_OUTP_HZ.summary: Output frequency of main SBF blocks
SEP_OUTP_HZ.description: The output frequency of the main SBF blocks needed for PVT information.

SEP_PITCH_OFFS.summary: Pitch offset for dual antenna GPS
SEP_PITCH_OFFS.description:
Vertical offsets can be compensated for by adjusting the Pitch offset.
Note that this can be interpreted as the "roll" angle in case the antennas are aligned along the perpendicular axis.
This occurs in situations where the two antenna ARPs may not be exactly at the same height in the vehicle reference frame.
Since pitch is defined as the right-handed rotation about the vehicle Y axis,
a situation where the main antenna is mounted lower than the aux antenna (assuming the default antenna setup) will result in a positive pitch.

SEP_SAT_INFO.description: Enable publication of satellite info (ORB_ID(satellite_info)) if possible.

SEP_STREAM_LOG.summary: Logging stream used during automatic configuration
SEP_STREAM_LOG.description:
The stream the autopilot sets up on the receiver to output the logging data.
Set this to another value if the default stream is already used for another purpose.

SEP_STREAM_MAIN.summary: Main stream used during automatic configuration
SEP_STREAM_MAIN.description:
The stream the autopilot sets up on the receiver to output the main data.
Set this to another value if the default stream is already used for another purpose.

SEP_YAW_OFFS.summary: Heading/Yaw offset for dual antenna GPS
SEP_YAW_OFFS.description:
Heading offset angle for dual antenna GPS setups that support heading estimation.
Set this to 0 if the antennas are parallel to the forward-facing direction
of the vehicle and the rover antenna is in front.
The offset angle increases clockwise.
Set this to 90 if the rover antenna is placed on the
right side of the vehicle and the moving base antenna is on the left side.

SIH_DISTSNSR_OVR.summary: if >= 0 the distance sensor measures will be overridden by this value
SIH_DISTSNSR_OVR.description: Absolute value superior to 10000 will disable distance sensor

SIH_IXX.description:
The inertia is a 3 by 3 symmetric matrix.
It represents the difficulty of the vehicle to modify its angular rate.

SIH_IXY.description:
The inertia is a 3 by 3 symmetric matrix.
This value can be set to 0 for a quad symmetric about its center of mass.

SIH_IXZ.description:
The inertia is a 3 by 3 symmetric matrix.
This value can be set to 0 for a quad symmetric about its center of mass.

SIH_IYY.description:
The inertia is a 3 by 3 symmetric matrix.
It represents the difficulty of the vehicle to modify its angular rate.

SIH_IYZ.description:
The inertia is a 3 by 3 symmetric matrix.
This value can be set to 0 for a quad symmetric about its center of mass.

SIH_IZZ.description:
The inertia is a 3 by 3 symmetric matrix.
It represents the difficulty of the vehicle to modify its angular rate.

SIH_KDV.description:
Physical coefficient representing the friction with air particules.
The greater this value, the slower the quad will move.
Drag force function of velocity: D=-KDV*V.
The maximum freefall velocity can be computed as V=10*MASS/KDV [m/s]

SIH_KDW.description:
Physical coefficient representing the friction with air particules during rotations.
The greater this value, the slower the quad will rotate.
Aerodynamic moment function of body rate: Ma=-KDW*W_B.
This value can be set to 0 if unknown.

SIH_LOC_H0.description:
This value represents the Above Mean Sea Level (AMSL) altitude where the simulation begins.
If using FlightGear as a visual animation,
this value can be tweaked such that the vehicle lies on the ground at takeoff.
LAT0, LON0, H0, MU_X, MU_Y, and MU_Z should ideally be consistent among each others
to represent a physical ground location on Earth.

SIH_LOC_LAT0.description:
This value represents the North-South location on Earth where the simulation begins.
LAT0, LON0, H0, MU_X, MU_Y, and MU_Z should ideally be consistent among each others
to represent a physical ground location on Earth.

SIH_LOC_LON0.description:
This value represents the East-West location on Earth where the simulation begins.
LAT0, LON0, H0, MU_X, MU_Y, and MU_Z should ideally be consistent among each others
to represent a physical ground location on Earth.

SIH_L_PITCH.description:
This is the arm length generating the pitching moment
This value can be measured with a ruler.
This corresponds to half the distance between the front and rear motors.

SIH_L_ROLL.description:
This is the arm length generating the rolling moment
This value can be measured with a ruler.
This corresponds to half the distance between the left and right motors.

SIH_MASS.description: This value can be measured by weighting the quad on a scale.

SIH_Q_MAX.description:
This is the maximum torque delivered by one propeller
when the motor is running at full speed.
This value is usually about few percent of the maximum thrust force.

SIH_T_MAX.description:
This is the maximum force delivered by one propeller
when the motor is running at full speed.
This value is usually about 5 times the mass of the quadrotor.

SIH_T_TAU.description: the time taken for the thruster to step from 0 to 100% should be about 4 times tau

SIM_AGP_FAIL.description:
Stuck: freeze the measurement to the current location
Drift: add a linearly growing bias to the sensor data

SIM_GPS_USED.summary: simulated GPS number of satellites used

SYS_AUTOCONFIG.description:
Set to 1 to reset parameters on next system startup (setting defaults).
Platform-specific values are used if available.
RC* parameters are preserved.

SYS_AUTOSTART.description: CHANGING THIS VALUE REQUIRES A RESTART. Defines the auto-start script used to bootstrap the system.

SYS_BL_UPDATE.description:
If enabled, update the bootloader on the next boot.
WARNING: do not cut the power during an update process, otherwise you will
have to recover using some alternative method (e.g. JTAG).
Instructions:
- Insert an SD card
- Enable this parameter
- Reboot the board (plug the power or send a reboot command)
- Wait until the board comes back up (or at least 2 minutes)
- If it does not come back, check the file bootlog.txt on the SD card

SYS_CAL_ACCEL.summary: Enable auto start of accelerometer thermal calibration at the next power up
SYS_CAL_ACCEL.description:
0 : Set to 0 to do nothing
1 : Set to 1 to start a calibration at next boot
This parameter is reset to zero when the temperature calibration starts.
default (0, no calibration)

SYS_CAL_BARO.summary: Enable auto start of barometer thermal calibration at the next power up
SYS_CAL_BARO.description:
0 : Set to 0 to do nothing
1 : Set to 1 to start a calibration at next boot
This parameter is reset to zero when the temperature calibration starts.
default (0, no calibration)

SYS_CAL_GYRO.summary: Enable auto start of rate gyro thermal calibration at the next power up
SYS_CAL_GYRO.description:
0 : Set to 0 to do nothing
1 : Set to 1 to start a calibration at next boot
This parameter is reset to zero when the temperature calibration starts.
default (0, no calibration)

SYS_CAL_TDEL.summary: Required temperature rise during thermal calibration
SYS_CAL_TDEL.description:
A temperature increase greater than this value is required during calibration.
Calibration will complete for each sensor when the temperature increase above the starting temperature exceeds the value set by SYS_CAL_TDEL.
If the temperature rise is insufficient, the calibration will continue indefinitely and the board will need to be repowered to exit.

SYS_CAL_TMAX.summary: Maximum starting temperature for thermal calibration
SYS_CAL_TMAX.description: Temperature calibration will not start if the temperature of any sensor is higher than the value set by SYS_CAL_TMAX.

SYS_CAL_TMIN.summary: Minimum starting temperature for thermal calibration
SYS_CAL_TMIN.description: Temperature calibration for each sensor will ignore data if the temperature is lower than the value set by SYS_CAL_TMIN.

SYS_DM_BACKEND.description:
If the board supports persistent storage (i.e., the KConfig variable DATAMAN_PERSISTENT_STORAGE is set),
the 'Default storage' backend uses a file on persistent storage. If not supported, this backend uses
non-persistent storage in RAM.

SYS_FAC_CAL_MODE.description:
If enabled, future sensor calibrations will be stored to /fs/mtd_caldata.
Note: this is only supported on boards with a separate calibration storage
/fs/mtd_caldata.

SYS_FAILURE_EN.description:
If enabled allows MAVLink INJECT_FAILURE commands.
WARNING: the failures can easily cause crashes and are to be used with caution!

SYS_HAS_BARO.summary: Control if the vehicle has a barometer
SYS_HAS_BARO.description:
Disable this if the board has no barometer, such as some of the Omnibus
F4 SD variants.
If disabled, the preflight checks will not check for the presence of a
barometer.

SYS_HAS_GPS.summary: Control if the vehicle has a GPS
SYS_HAS_GPS.description:
Disable this if the system has no GPS.
If disabled, the sensors hub will not process sensor_gps,
and GPS will not be available for the rest of the system.

SYS_HAS_MAG.summary: Control if and how many magnetometers are expected
SYS_HAS_MAG.description:
0: System has no magnetometer, preflight checks should pass without one.
1-N: Require the presence of N magnetometer sensors for check to pass.

SYS_HAS_NUM_ASPD.summary: Control if the vehicle has an airspeed sensor
SYS_HAS_NUM_ASPD.description:
Set this to 0 if the board has no airspeed sensor.
If set to 0, the preflight checks will not check for the presence of an
airspeed sensor.

SYS_HAS_NUM_DIST.summary: Number of distance sensors to check being available
SYS_HAS_NUM_DIST.description:
The preflight check will fail if fewer than this number of distance sensors with valid data is present.
Disable the check with 0.

SYS_HAS_NUM_OF.summary: Number of optical flow sensors required to be available
SYS_HAS_NUM_OF.description: The preflight check will fail if fewer than this number of optical flow sensors with valid data are present.

SYS_HITL.summary: Enable HITL/SIH mode on next boot
SYS_HITL.description:
While enabled the system will boot in Hardware-In-The-Loop (HITL)
or Simulation-In-Hardware (SIH) mode and not enable all sensors and checks.
When disabled the same vehicle can be flown normally.
Set to 'external HITL', if the system should perform as if it were a real
vehicle (the only difference to a real system is then only the parameter
value, which can be used for log analysis).

SYS_PARAM_VER.description:
This is used internally only: an airframe configuration might set an expected
parameter version value via PARAM_DEFAULTS_VER. This is checked on bootup
against SYS_PARAM_VER, and if they do not match, parameters are reset and
reloaded from the airframe configuration.

SYS_RGB_MAXBRT.description: Set to 0 to disable, 1 for maximum brightness
